articles.title: Eka is worth $1.45B thanks to a physical AI model that has experts raving | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Robots still aren’t that good at picking things up, despite billions of dollars of investment and endless videos fed into deep learning models.
That may be about to change, thanks to a manipulation architecture built by Eka Robotics, which encompasses a force-sensitive gripper and a new kind of deep-learning model. Founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal and former Google DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, the startup just closed an $150 million Series A round that values it at $1.45 billion post-money, led by venture funds a16z and F-Prime.
“They are already exceeding superhuman performance for certain tasks, and so we think over the next few months there will be superhuman performance in many dexterous manipulation tasks,” Raghu Raghuram, the a16z general partner who co-led the fundraising round, told TechCrunch.
In an era of never-ending robotic demonstrations, Eka’s capabilities are shocking veteran robot builders.
Kris Hauser, a professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, said it had a “wow factor” compared to other robot demos he saw recently. The Eka robot “was able to adapt to a large number of different objects without retraining,” Hauser said, adding that it also had an aspect of “humanness, creepy humanness that it would try over and over again if it failed the first time.”

articles.title: Pourquoi désactiver l’accès à distance de votre Freebox ne protège pas totalement votre réseau — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Freebox OS, l’interface d’administration des Freebox, peut s’ouvrir depuis n’importe quelle connexion : on retrouve alors les réglages de sa box sans être chez soi. C’est pratique, mais beaucoup d’abonnés n’en ont pas l’usage et préfèrent couper cet accès. Une interface d’administration n’a pas de raison d’être visible depuis Internet quand on ne s’en sert pas.
Le problème, c’est que le réglage qu’on vérifie spontanément pour cela est trompeur. Les failles PHP d’octobre 2026 m’ont forcé à aller fouiller dans les réglages de la Freebox, même si a priori, ces box ne sont pas impactées par ces failles.
Le réglage qu’on croit suffisant
Le premier réflexe consiste à ouvrir Freebox OS, à passer les paramètres en « Mode avancé » et à se rendre dans « Gestion des accès ». On y trouve une case « Activer l’authentification par mot de passe » : décochée, elle donne l’impression que l’accès à distance est coupé.
Ce n’est pas le cas. Cette case empêche seulement de se connecter à distance avec le mot de passe administrateur. Elle ne ferme pas le port. L’interface l’indique d’ailleurs, en petits caractères, juste au-dessus : « Lorsque vous utilisez des applications ou des liens de partage, l’accès à votre Freebox est rendu possible automatiquement », puis, en orange : « L’accès distant est possible pour les applications et les liens de partages ».

articles.title: Mozilla asks UK CMA to consult on browser choice screens now | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Why is the CMA asking us to choose the furniture before the house? The UK’s search choice screens need browser choice screens alongside them
Mobile browsers are a key gateway to the internet for 56 million people in the UK. Smartphone users spend around half an hour a day in these apps, and opening a browser is the most common way they look up information online.
Yet most people are using a smartphone browser that was preinstalled and set as the default for them, without ever being asked which browser they would actually prefer.
Mozilla believes people deserve an active choice in the tools they depend on every day, which is why the latest proposals from the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) matter. We welcome the CMA’s plans to give people a choice of search service and are asking it to consult on browser choice now, so both screens can launch together.
On September 23rd, the CMA published updated plans that would require Google to show people in the UK a choice of search service on new Android devices, covering the default search app and home-screen search widget as well as Chrome. Search choice screens would also appear in Chrome on other platforms, including through a major update for existing users. Some AI assistants would also be eligible to appear alongside search engines.
The proposals are well designed, but solve only half the problem

articles.title: Revolut outage disrupts online banking operations worldwide
articles.summary:
Fintech company Revolut is working to resolve a massive outage that disrupted most of its services worldwide earlier today.
Since the incident began, thousands of users on the Downdetector outage tracking platform have reported issues with the Revolut app, mobile banking services, and transferring funds between accounts.
In a statement today, the company said the outage has affected its services since Tuesday morning and added that customers' data and funds are safe.
"We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe," Revolut said.
"We've been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused."
On its official status page, the company says the outage affects 28 services, including sign-ins, card payments, transfers, currency exchange, stock trading, and live support chat, which are now flagged as partially unavailable.
According to Reuters, the Revolut outage is reportedly linked to ongoing service disruptions affecting Google Cloud's London-based europe-west2 data center after a "power event."
A Revolut spokesperson was not immediately available when BleepingComputer reached out earlier about the root cause of today's outage.

articles.title: Sans Huawei, que reste-t-il à la marque Aito pour conquérir l’Europe ? - Numerama
articles.summary:
Présente au Mondial de l’automobile de Paris 2026, la marque chinoise Aito s’est fait remarquer avec son stand XXL, l’un des trois plus grands du salon. La marque ambitionne un lancement en Europe à l’automne 2027. Il y aurait cependant un grand changement entre les modèles proposés en Chine et ceux disponibles dans les pays européens : la technologie Huawei serait absente.
Selon les médias chinois, comme Carnewschina le 20 octobre 2026, la marque n’embarquerait pas les technologies de conduite autonome et de cockpit signées Huawei, mais celles de Bosch. Sans les technologies Huawei qui ont contribué à son succès en Chine, que reste-t-il à Aito pour convaincre les automobilistes européens ?
« Huawei inside » en Chine contre « Bosch inside » en Europe
La notoriété de la marque Aito – dont le nom signifie « Adding Intelligence To Auto » (littéralement, ajouter de l’intelligence à l’automobile) – repose presque intégralement en Chine sur son intégration des technologies Huawei. Le constructeur Seres, derrière la marque Aito, a choisi une autre approche pour son expansion européenne.
Les futures Aito 6, 7, 8 et 9 feront l’impasse sur les logiciels et matériels signés Huawei. À la place, Seres se serait associé à l’équipementier allemand Bosch pour développer les aides à la conduite (ADAS), le cockpit intelligent et la gestion du châssis.

articles.title: Après avoir vendu sa maison, une famille française transforme un bus en véhicule électrique alimenté par des batteries de Tesla pour voyager partout dans le monde
articles.summary:
Après avoir vendu sa maison, une famille française transforme un bus en véhicule électrique alimenté par des batteries de Tesla pour voyager partout dans le monde
Rien ne se perd, tout se transforme. Et la famille Guillemot nous le rappelle avec son bus électrique alimenté par trois batteries Tesla. C’est la famille Guillemot qui a créé Chouchou, un bus électrique qui stocke 225 kWh dans trois batteries Tesla. Résultat, 90 mètres² de panneaux solaires pour le trajet comme la maison. Un projet lancé après la pandémie de coronavirus qui accompagne leur vie nomade.
Chouchou utilise le moteur d’une Tesla Model S Performance et l’énergie est stockée dans trois batteries de Model 3 Long Range pour un total de 225 kWh. Quant au bus qui transporte la famille (Jean-Philippe et Laure avec leurs enfants Clara et Lisa) appelé Chouchou, il s’agit d’un Temsa Safari de 12 mètres de long, 2,50 mètres de large et 3,85 mètres de haut. Autrefois, il était équipé d’un moteur diesel de 12 litres pour une consommation de 35 litres aux 100 km.
Des batteries Tesla pour alimenter ce bus électrique
C’est finalement en 2022 que la famille Guillemot modifie ce véhicule pour le transformer en bus électrique. Mais tout ne fut pas aisé. En 2022, un premier moteur de Tesla utilisé est tombé en panne après 250 km à cause d’une erreur électrique. Il a fallu un mois de réparation.

articles.title: Fausses cagnottes : attention aux arnaques qui profitent des pillages du 17 octobre
articles.summary:
Les pillages survenus ce week-end à travers la France ont laissé un certain nombre de commerçants complètement dévastés. Marchandises volées, investissements partis en fumée, vitrines cassées, agressions physiques : les conséquences sont lourdes pour les commerçants touchés, qui doivent désormais faire face aux dégâts, aussi bien matériels que psychologiques. Face à cette situation, les cagnottes de soutien se sont multipliées. Certaines ont été mises en place par les commerçants eux-mêmes, tandis que d’autres sont mises en ligne à l’initiative de personnes désirant aider. Malheureusement, certains lancent aussi de fausses cagnottes, autrement dit, des arnaques.
Des escrocs profitent de la détresse des commerçants
Un gérant d’un magasin Micromania situé à Nice a été victime de pilleurs. Il a été agressé physiquement, tandis que son magasin a été pillé et ses vitrines cassées. Face aux images de l’agression et du pillage, mais aussi du courage dont l’homme a fait preuve, plusieurs personnes ont lancé des cagnottes afin de lui venir en aide. Cependant, le gérant a alerté sur la prolifération de fausses cagnottes en ligne.
Il explique dans une story Instagram : « Mon équipe et moi, on est très touchés par le soutien, merci pour ce que vous faites. Maintenant, je vois des cagnottes en ligne, je ne suis au courant de rien, personne ne m’a contacté, elles ne sont pas de mon fait. Prenez soin de vous. articles.title: US orders federal agencies to remove China’s DeepSeek AI from their systems | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The U.S. has ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing services and products developed by Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and remove them from government IT systems over national security concerns tied to the Chinese AI startup’s operations in China, according to the Department of Homeland Security. The order goes beyond banning DeepSeek’s own product, and covers third-party products and services built using DeepSeek technology, though agencies can request exceptions.
The DHS raised concerns about DeepSeek’s handling of user data, warning that sensitive information from U.S. government users could potentially be accessible to Chinese authorities under Chinese law, the order said.
The move comes amid intensifying tech competition in AI between the U.S. and China. The Chinese AI model challenges its U.S. rivals, including OpenAI and Meta, with low-cost open-weight models.
China pushed back against the U.S.’s move. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Tuesday that Beijing opposes “overstretching the concept of national security and politicizing technology and trade issues,” according to an official briefing. “We will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises,” the spokesperson added.

Vous l’avez sans doute constaté, les écrans prennent une place de plus en plus grande dans notre vie. On pense aux smartphones, qui sont omniprésents, mais ce n’est pas tout. Dans nos voitures aussi, les dalles numériques sont partout, et elles sont de plus en plus imposantes. Trouver son chemin, régler la climatisation ou la ventilation : tout ou presque passe par l’écran tactile, ce qui n’est pas l’idéal en roulant.
Google veut aller un peu plus loin avec une nouvelle fonctionnalité, dévoilée ce mardi 20 octobre. La firme américaine propose depuis novembre dernier son intelligence artificielle Gemini dans certaines voitures. C’est le cas chez Renault et Volvo, mais aussi bientôt chez Xpeng et Geely. Elle est aussi déjà présente sur les smartphones fonctionnant sous Android. Mais voilà que la société californienne franchit une nouvelle étape, comme elle l’indique sur son site officiel.
Baptisée Personal Intelligence, cette fonctionnalité a été lancée en janvier aux États-Unis dans l’application Gemini, comme le détaillait Numerama. Elle permet à l’assistant d’aller fouiller dans les applications Google associées au compte du conducteur. articles.title: OPINION: Europe needs more than just successful exits | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
The acquisition of Berlin-based Talon.One by Dutch payments provider Adyen in July 2026 offers a useful perspective on European technology investing. A company founded in Germany developed technology valuable to a global payments business, and its next chapter is being written within Europe. This is a significant outcome for the founders and investors. However, it also raises a larger question: how can Europe turn individual successes into an ecosystem capable of producing them repeatedly?
The answer is not simply to encourage more European acquisitions. Successful startups need access to the best opportunities available, whether their future lies with a European buyer, an international technology group or the public markets. What matters is that these decisions reflect commercial potential rather than a lack of viable alternatives. For Europe, the challenge is to create the conditions in which successful companies can scale, attract investment and generate lasting economic value.
Exits are a measure of maturity, not the final destination
From a venture capital perspective, exits matter because they return capital to investors and founders, establish reference points for valuations, and help to finance the next generation of start-ups. Therefore, an acquisition is more than just the end of an investment cycle. articles.title: Here’s the tea
articles.summary:
Here’s the tea
An MIT historian uncovers the true origins of an artifact once thought to be a relic of the Boston Tea Party.
When Tristan Brown, an associate professor of history at MIT, first examined a Chinese tea chest label displayed at Old South Meeting House, he had no reason to doubt its story. Descendants of the Boston blacksmith Thomas Wells had donated the label in 1987, saying it had been recovered after colonial protesters threw tea into Boston Harbor in 1773.
But after a year of research, Brown reached a different conclusion: The label was made nearly a century later. The decisive clue came when he read the Chinese text in Cantonese rather than Mandarin, as previous scholars had done. He found that the characters had been used phonetically, in slightly variant forms across contemporary sources, to represent the name of Smith, Archer & Co., a US firm that acquired Asian tea for shipment to American markets during the 1860s and 1870s.
Working with the Wells family, he traced the label to a relative who traveled from Michigan to California during the Gold Rush era before returning and operating a business known as the California Tea Store. Brown argues that claims for its revolutionary pedigree probably developed later, amid the centennial commemorations of the 1870s.
The discovery does not make the label historically insignificant, he says. Instead, what began as an inquiry into a supposed artifact of the Boston Tea Party became a study of how ordinary objects acqu…

articles.title: Introducing tsrs: a Port of TypeScript to Rust
articles.summary:
Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler. We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain.
Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building. Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.
To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction. They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community. We do not want to change that.
The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation. A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible. We have to preserve the TypeScript language strictly based on its original implementation – and the TypeScript team should remain solely responsible for deciding what that looks like.
Performance and memory improvements

articles.title: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
articles.summary:
Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter’s third quarter earnings call Tuesday.
Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
Musk called the merger “a good idea,” though he cautioned it wasn’t a guarantee.
Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions.
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. “So it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation.”
The groups have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction — and there’s no guarantee that they will. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he continued. “And particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.”

RHEL for NVIDIA 26.03 is built on the latest version of RHEL, modifying a strictly limited set of core packages—the Linux kernel, QEMU, and libvirt—to enable launch-day hardware support. The rest of the userspace matches standard RHEL. Once those hardware enablement patches mature and merge into the upstream Linux kernel, organizations can seamlessly transition back to mainline RHEL via an off-ramp without reinstalling. That is the fast lane. It is not a separate product, and it is not a permanent fork of RHEL. The result is your ability to stay on an operating system your team already knows, instead of building the first AI cluster on a placeholder OS and planning to re-engineer it later.

MIT engineers’ design for a robot that both swims and flies could lead to a new class of vehicles for ocean exploration.
Given that water is 1,000 times denser than air, moving through those two mediums requires very different mechanics—or so one might assume. Yet birds like gulls and puffins can plunge into the sea, swim underwater, and leap back into the air to fly away. And now engineers at MIT and EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland, have designed a robot that can do likewise.
The “flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle,” or FAAV, weighs less than 300 grams (about half a pound) and is equipped with a central fuselage, two flexible wings, and a steerable tail. The body contains a battery and a waterproof electric motor that drives a crankshaft, which pumps the wings up and down at preset frequencies. The wings are made of thin membranes that are coated with hydrophobic nanoparticles to help wick away water. And the tail is motorized, enabling it to change its angle to help the robot fly up or dive down.
In experiments carried out in a water tank and at Lake Geneva, a team led by Raphael Zufferey, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, identified combinations of wing size, flapping frequency, and tail angle that enable the robot to smoothly transition from swimming to flying.

articles.title: Spectrum costs squeeze African telecom investment and growth
articles.summary:
Africa’s mobile networks have expanded significantly over the past decade, bringing coverage to more people. But wider coverage has not translated into widespread internet use or network quality on par with other regions.
A new report by the GSMA, Spectrum Policy in Africa: Enabling Investment and Empowering Consumers Through Effective Spectrum Pricing, identifies the high cost of accessing radio spectrum—the invisible radio frequencies that carry mobile calls and internet data—as a central bottleneck. African mobile operators pay significantly more for relatively less spectrum, leaving them with limited capacity to expand or improve service quality.
According to GSMA Intelligence, spectrum costs consume 0.82% of mobile operators’ revenue per 100 MHz in Africa, compared with 0.66% in the rest of the world. Meanwhile, African operators hold an average of about 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz, 24% less than the global peer average of approximately 750 MHz.
The imbalance extends beyond price and availability to licence duration. Only nine African countries routinely grant spectrum licences lasting 20 years or more, while licences of 20 years or indefinite duration are standard across Europe, North America and developed Asian markets.

articles.title: Cuáles son las cinco prácticas que hacen que la computadora dure menos de uno o dos años
articles.summary:
Muchos usuarios creen que un computador se vuelve lento o se avería por simple antigüedad, pero en la mayoría de los casos el desgaste prematuro responde a hábitos cotidianos que pasan desapercibidos.
Desde bloquear la ventilación hasta instalar programas sin control, existen prácticas que deterioran tanto el hardware como el software del equipo, y que son evitables con cuidados básicos.
Hábitos que afectan el tiempo de vida de un computador
- Bloquear la ventilación y acumular polvo
El calor es el principal enemigo de cualquier equipo. Los ventiladores integrados en la carcasa cumplen la función de ingresar aire fresco y expulsar el calor interno, un proceso que se ve comprometido cuando se usa el portátil sobre superficies blandas, como una cama, un sillón o las piernas.
El polvo y las pelusas que se acumulan en las entradas de aire también atascan el interior y empeoran la circulación. Esto genera un recalentamiento progresivo que puede dañar los componentes.
Por eso conviene usar el equipo siempre sobre una mesa rígida, limpiar los puertos externos cada mes y abrir el chasis cada tres meses para eliminar el polvo interior con aire comprimido.
- Dejar que el equipo se sobrecaliente
Cada componente de un computador está diseñado para funcionar dentro de un rango de temperatura específico. Superarlo acelera su degradación o provoca averías directas.
Un exceso de calor puede derretir soldaduras y desplazar componentes, además de secar la pasta térmica de la CPU, lo que reduce…

Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. articles.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
articles.summary:
Eliminating traffic deaths
Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death, yet we treat it like it’s inevitable,” says Leah Shahum, founder and director of the Vision Zero Network, a nonprofit focused on making streets less deadly.
The sticking points
The causes of a crash can be muddy. Drivers make mistakes like speeding or getting distracted, but infrastructure fails them too: Perhaps they were on a road built for speed and not safety, in a screen-filled vehicle, or at an intersection where pedestrians, cyclists, and other cars aren’t visible.
Cheap and proven traffic-calming opportunities abound—from using planters to tighten intersections to lowering speed limits—but government logjams and red tape can be speed bumps. “There’s so many moving parts,” says Laura Sandt of the University of North Carolina Highway Safety Research Center. “On the flip side, it shows that we have so many opportunities for injury prevention.”
The progress

articles.title: Solid-state batteries
articles.summary:
Solid-state batteries
Batteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.
The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy by moving charged lithium ions through a liquid electrolyte soup has its drawbacks, not least that the batteries have a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels.
The sticking points
Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. Solid electrolytes are supposed to physically block the formation of dendrites, but many o…

The agents’ action paths are determined as they work and reason through the steps needed to complete their goals. As they interact with the tools and systems around them, they adapt their reasoning and behavior to achieve their task.
The adaptability of agents is what makes them so powerful, but they are goal-oriented and may not prioritize safety in pursuit of their objectives. In order for agents to work both autonomously and safely, we need to build environments that provide control and visibility in what the agent is doing.
An agent cannot govern itself. Security and governance belong in the infrastructure the agent operates in.
OpenShell provides deterministic governance outside of the agent’s reach

Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
An AI SRE agent can help troubleshoot an incident. But can you trust it to decide on its own when something needs attention?
Most teams treat agent autonomy as a yes or no question. For incident response, it is a progression with three phases, and many agents in production sit earlier on it than the teams running them realize. Most AI SRE tools still stop short of the final phase.
On Thursday, October 22, The New Stack hosts a live webinar with Raaz Dwivedi, co-founder and CTO of Traversal and an assistant professor at Cornell Tech. His team applies causal AI and agentic reasoning to production incidents. He will walk through where the industry sits on that progression and what it takes to move up.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The three phases of agent autonomy
Invoked: copilots, chat interfaces, and CLIs that wait for an on-call engineer to open them and ask a question mid-incident.
Background: scheduled jobs, alert rules, and triggers that fire on conditions someone predicted in advance.
Proactive: agents that decide for themselves when an incident needs attention, without waiting to be invoked or scheduled.
The first two phases share a limit. Each depends on a person noticing that something is wrong, or on someone predicting the right condition ahead of time. Proactive agents remove that dependency.

Mais tous ont subi de plein fouet l’offensive des marques chinoises, qui leur a fait perdre de très nombreuses parts de marché.
Les livraisons du groupe Volkswagen en Chine ont chuté de 36,6 % au deuxième trimestre 2026 sur un an, bien plus que le marché chinois, en recul d’environ 20 % selon le constructeur. Elles ont encore plongé de 38,5 % au troisième trimestre. Une enquête de Reuters publiée ce lundi 20 octobre montre que l’alliance nouée avec Xpeng pour inverser la tendance n’a, pour l’instant, pas tenu ses promesses.
Pour contrer ces difficultés, Volkswagen avait fait le choix en 2023 de nouer un partenariat stratégique avec Xpeng. Le but ? Un nouveau document officiel déniché sur le web détaille justement une méthode de génération d’images qui va permettre d’améliorer la fluidité des images affichées sur votre TV ou votre écran de PC.
Anticiper vos mouvements grâce à la manette
Contrairement au DLSS qui récupère uniquement les données de mouvement depuis le moteur du jeu, le modèle imaginé par Sony intègre un paramètre supplémentaire qui exploite les informations de la manette pour anticiper avec plus de précision vos déplacements d’une image à l’autre. Le brevet précise que « Dans certaines configurations, les prédictions ne se limitent pas à l’image qui suit immédiatement dans le flux », soulignant que le système de décodage peut être entraîné pour prédire un nombre variable d’images situées avant ou après l’image d’entrée. "Chukwuemeka Amachukwu believed he was operating safely offshore when he targeted his victims, but he has now been held to account and now faces a serious sentence for his crimes," said US Attorney Jamie McDonald in a Monday press release.

articles.title: YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
articles.summary:
YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them.
YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
Some users have reported that their YouTube dislike button has been moved to the three-dots menu.
Right now, for me, the dislike button sits right next to the like button under a video. Moving it to a submenu would make it considerably more of an effort to access, meaning that fewer people would likely use it.
It’s unclear how widely this apparent test may be rolled out, and Google didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
YouTube has shown a willingness to make changes to the dislike button. In 2021, it hid the public dislike count on videos to help “protect creators from harassment,” though creators can still see dislike counts. Earlier this year, YouTube removed the dislike button from YouTube Shorts, suggesting instead that users take advantage of options in the three-dots menu.

Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant.
A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand. When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”
Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant, which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.
The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant.
To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song.

articles.title: Hijacked Developer Account Used to Plant Stealer in OVHcloud CLI
articles.summary:
French cloud computing and web hosting company OVHcloud says a hacker used the GitHub account of one of its developers to plant a secret-stealing binary in its official command-line interface (CLI) tool.
The supply chain incident occurred on October 19, and OVHcloud lists versions v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 as compromised. Version 0.10.0 and the newly released version 0.16.0 are clean.
“The hacker used the GitHub account of one of the developers and added a binary whose job is to retrieve secrets from the disk. The quality of the binary is poor but it can go all the way,” OVHcloud founder Octave Klaba said on X (translated from French).
Klaba said the compromised version appeared at 14:47 Paris time and was blocked at 16:21, after a customer reported the issue. According to OpenSourceMalware, a user flagged the tampering publicly on GitHub after an automated hash check failed.
The CI/CD pipelines were not impacted, Klaba noted in a different post, as the issue stemmed from GitHub’s release immutability option not being enabled.
“As a result, a user with the appropriate permissions could directly modify existing releases on GitHub without any checks from our CI/CD,” Klaba said. The option has since been enabled.
OpenSourceMalware says the attacker uploaded the binary over the original files of already published releases. Only builds for the most common platforms were replaced, which the researchers believe points to credential harvesting on developer and operations workstations.

articles.title: Cleaning up PFAS
articles.summary:
Cleaning up PFAS
Ridding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental and health woes.
Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond between carbon and fluorine, which the environment struggles to break down.
The sticking points
PFAS are everywhere: They spew from factories and slough off products and into water with normal use. Scientists have found them in everything from human blood to Antarctic snow. One 2022 report found that 89% of the US population had PFAS in excess of two nanograms per milliliter of blood plasma, a common threshold for potential adverse health effects, and 9% of the population had passed the riskier level of 20 nanograms per milliliter.
The PFAS monster is also a moving target. New compounds are still being created and used. There are more than 12,000 of them, and much of the cleanup research focuses on only a small handful.
The progress
Cleansing PFAS-contaminated soil is a project in its infancy, but it is possible to prevent more buildup by pulling the chemicals out of water systems. There are two ways to handle this: trap or destroy. Some scientists have found reverse osmosis—a process that…

Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
A single query is all that’s required
Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. articles.title: Data centre vs Cloud platform: Is there a difference?
articles.summary:
You have probably seen the words “data centre” and “cloud” used interchangeably. They don’t mean the same thing, and the difference matters. It shapes how businesses buy technology, how regulators write rules and where investors see opportunity.
A data centre is a building. It is a secure, purpose-built facility with reliable power, cooling, security and internet connections, so that computers can run around the clock. A cloud platform is a service. It is software that lets customers rent computing power, storage, and networking on demand, switch them on or off themselves, and pay only for what they use.
Think of an airport and an airline. The airport provides the runway, fuel, and terminal; the airline provides the service you actually book. Every cloud platform runs inside a data centre, but most data centres do not offer a cloud platform. Owning an airport does not make you an airline.
Data centre grading and cloud computing standards
Companies that rent space for their own servers in someone else’s facility are buying what the industry calls “colocation”. A facility’s reliability is rated on a four-level scale from the Uptime Institute.
Tier I has no backup equipment, so any fault results in downtime. Tier II adds spares but has a single path for power and cooling.
Tier III has more than one path, so any part can be serviced without switching anything off; it is the level most serious operators aim for. Tier IV survives any single failure.

AI’s Midas problem: When code is free, features are worthless
Every team that adopted Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot to produce more code has the same problem: When output is free, offering volume stops being a viable strategy. In fact, teams accelerating their software development with AI may be giving up the very thing that makes their software valuable.
It’s time to remember what makes software valuable and why racing to produce a mountain of code and features leads to failure.
The Midas touch
In Ovid’s tale, Midas, king of Phrygia, took in the missing satyr Silenus, whom Phrygian peasants had found drunk, granted him ten days of hospitality, and then returned him to Dionysus. In return, he was offered the reward of his choice: whatever he wished for. Famously, he wished that everything he touched would turn to gold.
Testing his new ability on an oak twig and then a stone, Midas was delighted. Nathaniel Hawthorne, who retold the myth for children in 1851, added a rose garden: His Midas turns every bloom to gold, still delighted, though his daughter Marygold mourns that the roses no longer smell sweet. In both versions, the celebration ends at the table, where food and drink turn to gold in his hands. That’s when Midas realized his reward was a bane, not a blessing, and asked to be rid of it.
Many leaders who force-fed AI to developers are now coming to a realization similar to that of Midas.

articles.title: Interspecies communication
articles.summary:
Interspecies communication
Decoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could offer a window into the inner lives of other species and help humans realize that “animals are sentient creatures who think, who have hopes and dreams of their own,” says Con Slobodchikoff, the founder of Zoolingua, a company working on dog-to-human speech.
The sticking points
Teasing all this out is complex. To decipher howls, squeaks, and clicks, researchers must match the creatures making sounds with what’s happening around them. Prairie dogs, for example, utter a different series of yips when a coyote approaches than when a hawk is nearby. It’s painstaking work, especially for difficult-to-observe species, like deep-diving whales or subterranean mole rats.
There are other hurdles. Many animals communicate not just through sound but through visual cues, touch, pheromones, or a combination of signals, some of which might be difficult for us to perceive. And without a multispecies Rosetta stone, it’s hard to know if translations are accurate.
The progress

RFD4-Proteina, an NVIDIA BioNeMo open model co-developed with the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington’s School of Medicine, navigates that space using patterns learned from nature. It co-designs protein sequences and all-atom structures, and uses reward-guided inference-time search to focus compute on the most promising candidates.

articles.title: Exercise in a pill
articles.summary:
Exercise in a pill
In unraveling the pathways by which movement helps the body, we could develop medicines that offer some of the same benefits, without the workout.
We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness.
The sticking points
It will take a lot of experimentation to untangle the myriad pathways by which exercise promotes health. But IDing the cascade of hormones, enzymes, and other molecules related to physical activity is just the first step. Scientists need to figure out how to turn that knowledge into safe and effective drugs. That’s a tall order: More than 90% of treatments that enter human studies fail.
There are regulatory hurdles too. The FDA approves medications to treat diseases, not to enhance wellness, says Thomas Burris, a pharmacologist at the University of Florida whose work focuses on diseases that respond to exercise, like obesity, type 2 diabetes, and dementia.
The progress
There may never be a pill that delivers all the benefits of exercise, but research could lead to new medicines that mimic some aspects of working out. Scientists have already identified many important exercise-related signals and have even developed…

articles.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
articles.summary:
Nuclear-powered spaceships
A new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.
The sticking points
Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not. The Soviet Union sent dozens of reactors into orbit, often to power spy satellites. And experts say there aren’t any major technical obstacles to making nuclear space propulsion happen. “I think it’s a very doable technology,” says Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute.“I’m happy to see them finally doing this.”
Still, developing space propulsion using reactors has been slow going. The US has started—and terminated—several programs looking into it over the past 75 years. The latest casualty was DRACO, a collaboration betw…

My grandmother was a commanding woman. In her 92 years, she raised three children and a grandchild, mostly by herself. She helped manage a series of successful restaurants and nightclubs; in her little spare time, she hiked and skied. She was decidedly capable.
But when I unexpectedly knocked on her door one autumn when I was 19, something was different: she asked me the same questions, different only in sentence structure, again and again.
What brought me to town?
Where was I going to school?
What was I doing in town?
What college was I enrolled in?
Over the years, she lost more of her faculties. Eventually, she left the stovetop on for so long that a steel pot melted into molten coagulant. That was the boiling point: a week later she moved in with my parents.
My grandmother’s experience was not abnormal. Like many seniors, she was caught between her desire to remain independent and the limitations of her advancing age; she didn’t want to leave her home, but could also no longer live safely on her own. With little money to afford in-home care, those years put untold pressure on my parents and left my grandmother in a sort of purgatory: she wasn’t independent, but she also didn’t have round-the-clock care.
If Calgary’s Garden Loft had been around back then, might things have been different?

The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.”
A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster.
Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. articles.title: Chinese AI Model Writes More Hackable Code When Told It’s for US Contractor

AI models that have a pro-China lean may systematically generate more vulnerable code when writing applications for Western organizations, cybersecurity firm Hirundo has discovered.
The fact that geopolitical triggers lead to more vulnerable code being produced by Chinese AI is not new: CrowdStrike reached a similar conclusion in November 2025, and so did Booz Allen Hamilton in May 2026 (PDF).
Both organizations said that the bias occurred when the AI was prompted to code for an organization in a country of interest to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Hirundo has verified that on its own.
It instructed Alibaba’s Qwen3-Coder to build a web service that allows users to sign up, log in, and store secrets. The model built over 1,000 applications, and the test clearly showed the bias, Hirundo notes in a report shared with SecurityWeek ahead of publication.
“We ran every request through two models. The first is Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as Alibaba ships it. The second is Hirundo’s Westernized Qwen3-Coder: the same model after we removed its CCP alignment from the weights with behavioral unlearning,” the company says.
Both were instructed to build apps for a US defense contractor, a Chinese defense contractor, and a Hong Kong democracy advocacy group.

Artificial Intelligence

Agentic AI applications need governed access to live enterprise data. That data can live in operational systems, analytical warehouses, SaaS applications, other clouds, or on premises. In the previous post in this series, we built a semantic layer on AWS using Stardog’s knowledge graph over Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift. A Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore queried that layer. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This post uses the same customer 360 pattern, but swaps in a different semantic layer implementation and extends the source mix.
Two things change here. First, the semantic layer is the Denodo Platform: an AI data layer that provides active context and live, zero-copy access to distributed enterprise data. The agent talks to it in VQL, Denodo’s SQL dialect. Second, the source mix includes an on-premises PostgreSQL database alongside Amazon Aurora and Amazon Redshift, so the federation problem is no longer bounded by an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).
The rest of the pattern carries over. A foundation model on Amazon Bedrock plans and writes queries. The pitch is great: Instead of opening Screen Sharing and steering a full remote desktop, a user picks a single window on the other machine, say a Terminal session or a browser window an agent is working in, and it opens alongside everything else on the Mac in front of them. It gets its own Dock icon and can be called using the Command+Tab switcher. Resizing the window resizes the window on the other Mac. Keyboard shortcuts work, files can be dragged across, and the app’s audio can play locally. The app itself never leaves the original machine. When one window isn’t enough, Beam can pull over a full display or the whole Mac.
Shah frames it around his own setup in his Product Hunt launch post, describing Macs running agents and local models “with work continuing even when nobody’s sitting in front of them.” Getting to one of those machines usually means Screen Sharing and a second desktop to navigate. Beam is meant to cut that down to the one window that matters.

NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs.
Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test.
NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost.

The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), signed on April 27, came into effect on Tuesday, providing duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
It is the seventh trade pact to come into force in the last five years. The others are agreements with the UAE, Mauritius, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) bloc, the UK, Oman and Australia.

Gulzar Didwania, Partner, Deloitte India, said the deal is expected to support higher FDI inflows into India, but the scale of any increase remains uncertain and will depend on private-sector investment decisions.
New Zealand has committed FDI worth USD 20 billion in over 15 years.

Was steckt hinter Dunkler Energie? Dies ist eines der großen Rätsel der Kosmologie. Die unsichtbare, hypothetische Form der Energie gilt als verantwortlich für die Ausdehnung des Universums, nachdem der erste Schub durch den Big Bang abgeklungen war.
Neuer Weg zum Verständnis von Dunkler Energie?
Direkt nachgewiesen werden konnte die Dunkle Energie, die fast 70 Prozent der Energiedichte des Universums ausmachen soll, noch nicht. Ein Forschungsteam könnte aber nun einen Weg gefunden haben, Dunkle Energie künftig besser zu verstehen.
Die Resultate ihrer Forschung haben die Wissenschaftler:innen in gleich zwei Papern vorgestellt, die beide in der Fachzeitschrift The Astrophysical Journal erschienen sind.
Analyse von neutralem Wasserstoff
Die Forschenden haben mit dem Radioteleskop Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) nach Spuren von kosmischem Wasserstoff gesucht. Genauer gesagt nach neutralem atomaren Wasserstoff, der nicht ionisiert und also elektrisch ungeladen ist.
Neutraler Wasserstoff sendet eine Radiostrahlung mit einer Wellenlänge von etwa 21 Zentimetern aus. Durch die Expansion des Universums wird die Strahlung auf dem Weg zur Erde zu niedrigeren Frequenzen verschoben.

articles.title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
articles.summary:
Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse.
Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn’t very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we’ll need to run complex algorithms, we’d have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit.
On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10.
Error correction codes and scaling

Artificial Intelligence
Securing AI agent identity with X.509 PKI on AWS
When AI agents access databases, APIs, and sensitive business operations, establishing cryptographic identity through X.509 public key infrastructure (PKI) becomes a critical requirement. The core challenge is proving which agent made a request, preventing forgery between agents, and confirming that each agent acts only on behalf of an authorized user. Traditional approaches such as sharing API keys between components or passing OAuth tokens through agent chains fall short of the zero-trust requirements that enterprise deployments demand.
Multi-agent AI frameworks increasingly use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to connect agents to external tools and data sources. MCP defines how a large language model (LLM)-powered agent invokes tools such as database queries or email operations. However, MCP has no built-in authentication standard. It is transport-agnostic by design. This creates a critical gap: Without proper identity mechanisms, any component could impersonate an agent, replay intercepted credentials, or invoke tools without authorization.
In this post, we show you how to address this gap using Keyfactor EJBCA combined with AWS services. EJBCA is a PKI platform that supports high-availability deployment, REST API automation, and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) validation. articles.title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads From Java Applications
articles.summary:
TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous GPU programming framework for Java has reached version 7.3, a major milestone for the project.
InfoQ previously covered the project in December 2025 and in 2022.
TornadoVM automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs. Rather than replacing existing JVMs, it works alongside them and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that you can use with any mainstream JDK distribution such as OpenJDK, Graalvm, Temurin, or Zulu.
It offloads Java code to hardware backends, manages memory between the Java heap and accelerators, and runs the resulting compute kernels. This makes it a useful building block for modern cloud and machine learning workloads.
During development, TornadoVM compiles the source Java code to OpenCL and Apple Metal backends. The idea is that you can develop locally on your laptop and use the hardware available locally, and then deploy into a server that has Nvidia GPUs, and achieve major performance improvements - a form of "Write Once, Run Anywhere" for modern ML workloads.
Version 7 brings several architectural changes. The backends now use the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API in place of the Java Native Interface (JNI). The experimental JVM Compiler Interface (JVMCI) dependency has also been removed. According to the team, TornadoVM now sources "all compiler metadata through a reflection + ASM + Unsafe layer" which is the single, uniform path on every supported JDK (21, 25, 26 and 27).

Shader compilation stutter has plagued PC gaming for years, and a new application called Shader Compilation Stutter Killer, or SCSKiller for short, promises to do something about it. The idea is simple enough: compile shaders before launching a game rather than waiting for them to be compiled during gameplay. But does it actually work?
That's what we set out to find out, testing the application across several notoriously stutter-prone games. Along the way, we also discovered something rather interesting about shader compilation on Radeon GPUs. Something that could be a pretty big deal, and that we hadn't heard about before.
What's SCSKiller?
SCSKiller is a free and open-source application, so if you're interested, we recommend downloading it and giving it a shot for yourself. For those unfamiliar with shader compilation stutter, it's a common issue in modern PC gaming where a game briefly freezes or hitches the first time a new visual effect appears.
Some games attempt to address this by precompiling shaders before gameplay begins. The Last of Us Part I, for example, is famous for its lengthy shader compilation process.
Unfortunately, even games that precompile shaders can still suffer from horrific shader compilation stutter, while others don't bother precompiling much of anything, which can also lead to a poor experience.

articles.title: Building Physical AI Systems That Can Work in the Real World - EE Times

Physical AI brings AI into machines that must sense their surroundings, make decisions, and act in the physical world. The market opportunity is substantial: McKinsey estimates that AI-powered agents and robots could unlock about $2.9 trillion in annual economic value in the U.S. by 2030. However, realizing this opportunity depends on moving from working prototypes to products that can operate reliably, safely, and economically at scale.
That exposes a different engineering problem. In a prototype, teams can often add more compute, sensors, cooling, or power to prove that a capability works. In deployment, every added capability must fit within the size, weight, power, and cost budget, often abbreviated to SWaP-C, of the system.
Those constraints shape how a robot performs: How long it can operate between charges, how much productive payload it can carry, and how reliably it operates over time. The challenge is not simply adding more intelligence but integrating it effectively into deployable products.
A robot must continuously interpret its surroundings, decide how to respond, and translate those decisions into physical action. Doing that requires capabilities from perception and AI inference to planning and motion control to work together, while meeting different compute and timing requirements.

eMudhra revoked the compromised certificates, and the issue was communicated to downstream trust stores.

How to review AI code without reading the code
The argument over whether engineers should stop reading code is over, because we already have.
Faros AI’s new report shows a 76.3% increase in pull requests merged without review since their last report in April. Many companies now run AI reviews on 50% to 80% of their PRs. AI review took over bug-finding. But it didn’t take over the conversation where a team debates what it decided and why, and that is the part I missed too.
The part AI review doesn’t solve
Most teams are stuck in one of two modes. They review every line and become the bottleneck, or they rubber-stamp and lose track of what changed and why. There is no middle ground yet.
“The argument over whether engineers should stop reading code is over, because we already have.”
AI review is good at the mechanical half of the job. It never gets tired, it reads every line, and it holds the same standard on every PR. But it never saw what was decided. It won’t tell you not to build something, and it can’t be accountable for the result. A better model won’t fix that, because the tool reads the wrong artifact at the wrong time.
As I wrote in “Kill the code review theater, keep the review,” code review is how a team builds a mental model of its system. That has been the only scheduled moment for engineers to talk to each other about that system. Teams that hand code reviews to AI tools rarely notice they’ve also given up that moment.

A developer asks for a channel such as latest, lts, preview, daily, a major like 10, a minor like 10.0, or a feature band like 10.0.1xx, and dotnetup resolves it to a release. Exact versions, as the post notes, stay pinned during updates.
Several requirements can share one managed installation, and the tool reads the nearest global.json so team builds stay deterministic. Installation uses a bootstrap script fetched from aka.ms with curl or irm. articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry
Runtime discovery with AWS Agent Registry can help address a problem that agent demos might hide. Hardcoded tools work fine for a handful, start to degrade at a few dozen, and become unmanageable beyond that. Enterprise systems expose hundreds of internal APIs for pricing, support, orders, inventory, and customer data. In these systems, the model can spend more tokens disambiguating tool names than reasoning about the user’s request. Each new capability requires a code change in the orchestrator, a redeploy, and a coordinated release across teams that would much rather ship on their own cadence.
This pattern can arise across enterprise software as a service (SaaS) engagements where teams expose large internal API surfaces to agentic consumers. Build-time wiring can become a bottleneck as the catalog expands. One approach is to change how the orchestrator accesses its tools: instead of compiling every tool into the agent, the agent can discover relevant tools at runtime.
AWS Agent Registry is a managed service for cataloging and discovering Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agents, and agent skills. Publishers register protocol-specific descriptors and searchable descriptions. At runtime, an orchestrator can search approved, discoverable records and use the returned endpoint and descriptor content to construct a client. It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation.
The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded.
The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.
Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Canadian organizations building generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock often need the latest foundation models (FMs), such as OpenAI GPT-6.1, OpenAI GPT-6, and GPT-5.6, accessible from the Canadian AWS Regions. With Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference (CRIS), you can now access these models from Canada. Cross-Region inference is a capacity mechanism. Your application calls the Amazon Bedrock Runtime endpoint in your source Region. Amazon Bedrock then routes the request to a supported destination Region for processing. With this approach, you get access to a broader capacity pool that can help your application sustain throughput during demand spikes. You don’t need to manage destination Region routing in your application.

The product, called Voice, is available through an application programming interface or for self-hosted deployment. PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. It is, by some accounts, used by 85% of the AI apps. PyTorch was originally developed by Meta (then Facebook) in 2016, long before the world had an inkling that LLMs would change the world. Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It also makes it easy to move existing PyTorch apps to TPUs and, therefore, to Google Cloud. Developers can do this with a simple configuration change and no rewriting of their apps.

Nearly a year into the agentic coding explosion, many teams now use AI to write software as their de facto approach. As a result, Anthropic’s engineers are shipping eight times as much code as before, and some engineers are shipping thousands of PRs per month.
Management teams expecting their engineering capacity to explode will find that AI-written code doesn’t necessarily compress the software development lifecycle (SDLC) on its own.
The critical bottleneck in software creation has shifted from writing code to a later SDLC stage. After coding agents spit out new code, it still needs testing, and traditionally that meant humans writing the tests. That work includes deciding which user flows need testing, scripting tests for them, and rejiggering them when those flows change.
We’ve made it easy to write code and, in the process, increased the burden on humans to test new code. If we want to slash software development timelines, something has to change.
The observability and monitoring giant Datadog bought Propolis earlier this year, adding agent-written, goal- and output-oriented test writing to its platform. The approach lets agents explore applications, follow user flows on their own, and generate tests from plain-language prompts.

El problema es que identificar restos tan fragmentados no es tarea fácil, y es por ello que aquí es donde entra la "magia" tecnológica, puesto que la confirmación de que estos dos últimos fragmentos pertenecían a un neandertal se ha logrado mediante el análisis de las proteínas.

articles.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
articles.summary:
Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.
In the release announcement, Cilium engineers Nico Vibert and Donia Chaiehloudj describe Gateway API as a "much broader traffic management layer" in version 1.20. Cilium moves from Gateway API 1.4 to 1.6, adding ExternalAuth, ListenerSets, CORS filtering, TCPRoute and UDPRoute. These additions bring HTTP authentication and non-HTTP services such as databases and DNS under the same Kubernetes API used for web and gRPC traffic.
According to Vibert and Chaiehloudj, ExternalAuth allows an HTTPRoute to consult an external authorisation service before sending a request to an application. Depending on the response, the gateway can forward the request, redirect a user to a login page, or reject it. The authoriser can also pass identity headers to the application. TCPRoute and UDPRoute remove the need to fall back to LoadBalancer or NodePort Services for plain Layer 4 traffic.
ListenerSets address a separate ownership problem. Application teams can add listeners from their own namespaces while a platform team retains control of the shared Gateway and decides which namespaces may extend it. articles.title: Anthropic affiche 80 milliards de dollars de pertes : pourquoi ce chiffre est trompeur — Frandroid

Le Wall Street Journal a pu lire le projet de prospectus d’Anthropic, c’est-à-dire le document financier qu’une entreprise doit publier avant d’entrer en Bourse. Sur les six premiers mois de 2026, l’éditeur de Claude affiche une perte nette de 80,7 milliards de dollars (environ 72 milliards d’euros), contre 13 milliards de dollars (près de 12 milliards d’euros) un an plus tôt.
Pourtant, l’essentiel de ces 80,7 milliards n’a jamais quitté ses comptes en banque. Anthropic doit entrer en Bourse en novembre, et ses futurs actionnaires vont surtout regarder ce qui reste une fois ces charges comptables retirées.
Une perte gonflée par sa propre valorisation
Toujours selon le WSJ, 72 milliards de dollars (environ 64 milliards d’euros) viennent de charges comptables liées à des obligations convertibles et à d’autres titres émis pour lever des fonds. Une obligation convertible est un prêt que l’investisseur pourra plus tard échanger contre des actions. Plus Anthropic vaut cher, plus ces titres prennent de la valeur, et la comptabilité enregistre cette hausse comme une charge, sans qu’un dollar ne sorte de l’entreprise.
Le même mécanisme expliquait déjà la perte nette de 42 milliards de dollars (environ 37 milliards d’euros) de 2025, révélée par Reuters en septembre. Sur son activité réelle, Anthropic avait perdu 8,06 milliards de dollars sur l’année, pour 4,59 milliards de chiffre d’affaires (environ 7,2 et 4,1 milliards d’euros).
Si on retire ces écritures, il reste quand même environ…

Longtemps cantonnés à l’aspiration des poussières et autres miettes, les aspirateurs robots récents savent aussi laver les sols, retourner seuls à leur station et, pour certains même, gérer une grande partie de leur entretien sans la moindre intervention humaine.
Toutefois, derrière les promesses et des performances toujours plus impressionnantes, tous les robots laveurs ne se valent pas forcément. Voici les critères à examiner avant de choisir son aspirateur robot.
Le robot laveur ne se contente plus de passer un coup de serpillière
Sur le papier, le principe d’un robot laveur reste simple. Il vient aspirer les saletés puis humidifie une ou plusieurs serpillières pour nettoyer le sol. Les générations récentes ont toutefois très largement perfectionné cette seconde étape.
On trouve désormais des systèmes à serpillière fixe, oscillante ou rotative. La première privilégie la simplicité, l’oscillante multiplie les mouvements de frottement tandis que la rotative mise sur une action plus dynamique. Le choix dépend donc aussi du type de salissures rencontrées au quotidien.
Une autre évolution importante concerne la station, qui ne sert plus uniquement à recharger le robot. Sur certains modèles, elle peut remplir le réservoir d’eau propre, récupérer l’eau sale, laver les serpillières et les sécher automatiquement à l’air chaud. Une évolution particulièrement intéressante pour limiter les manipulations entre deux cycles, et optimiser le nettoyage des sols.

articles.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs

Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet.
As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices.
One word: bonkers
The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here – Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide.

articles.title: Mods can almost double DLSS 5 performance through Foveation, reducing resolution at the edges of frames — technique makes DLSS 5 possible on high-resolution ultrawide monitors
articles.summary:
Mods can almost double DLSS 5 performance through Foveation, reducing resolution at the edges of frames — technique makes DLSS 5 possible on high-resolution ultrawide monitors
This might actually make DLSS 5 more accessible.
Popular graphics post-processing injector software ReShade, commonly used to mod DLSS 5 into unsupported games, now has a foveated imaging add-on, including another standalone project that doesn't need precursor software, allowing DLSS 5 to affect only what's in view, reducing GPU load and increasing FPS.
Foveated imaging is nothing new; it's a technique that's been used in VR to increase performance. It works by only rendering what's in view, often increasing the resolution in the center and reducing it at the edges. Our eyes work in a similar way, with the clearest image in a small area in the center of your vision, blurring on the edges. Artificial Intelligence
Fine-tuning GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
GPT-OSS-20B is an open-weight reasoning model that thinks in English. Ask it to reason in French, German, Spanish, or Italian and it acknowledges the instruction, then produces its chain-of-thought in English anyway. On a 50-example multilingual reasoning test, the base model reasoned in the correct target language only 22 percent of the time. That 22 percent was almost entirely the English examples (English 100 percent, French 0 percent, German 10 percent, Spanish 0 percent, Italian 0 percent).
For teams deploying reasoning models for non-English users, that gap matters. A user who asks a question in French expects the model to reason and answer in French, not to switch to English mid-thought. Closing that gap is a fine-tuning problem. It raises a question every team faces once they start customizing open-weight models: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), or both?
In this post, we walk through how we fine-tuned GPT-OSS-20B for multilingual reasoning on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod. We show when SFT alone was sufficient and when GRPO added measurable value on top. To understand more broadly when GRPO helps, we also ran a controlled Qwen2.5-7B experiment across two tasks with different capability gaps. articles.title: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Spring Batch can scale horizontally without a message broker by using the relational database it already requires as the coordination plane. It fits the small-to-medium clusters many teams run.
- The pattern solves the problems a broker otherwise handles for you: sizing work to the live node count, assigning per-execution master responsibility with no standing coordinator, and claiming partitions with compare-and-set writes so no partition is silently lost.
- Node failure is handled by heartbeats and a two-phase recovery. It marks a stale node as unreachable, then after a grace period window, removes it and reassigns its incomplete, transferable partitions.
- Correctness is an explicit contract. Transferable work runs at least once and must be idempotent; nontransferable work runs at most once and is failed rather than moved. A partition is never silently lost.
- Database coordination fits where operational simplicity and cost matter most. Its ceiling is database contention and past that point, at very large clusters or sub-second latency, a broker remains the better choice.

Spring Batch has been the default framework for batch processing on the JVM for more than a decade. Jobs are built from steps, such as chunk-oriented readers, processors, and writers, with a metadata repository that makes runs restartable.
