Certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers found their private keys were so weak that anyone could recover them almost instantly and use them to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites.
Major browsers and operating systems trusted the compromised certificates, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications.
A security researcher known as Wayne discovered the weakness on October 17 while scanning publicly available certificate data.
According to Mozilla's incident report, all eight certificates used P-384 private keys generated in April 2025 that had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers.
To demonstrate the weakness, security researcher Flüpke published one of the compromised private keys on GitHub, showing that the private key for eMudhra's "EM OV TLS CA - G3C" certificate had a value of just 4.
BleepingComputer independently verified that the published key matches one of the revoked certificates.
In a response to Mozilla, eMudhra blamed the issue on an error in a script used to generate the certificates in April 2025. The company said the error generated a second set of weaker keys that were mistakenly selected for certificate signing because they had labels similar to the properly generated keys.
Some of the resulting certificates were also submitted to Sectigo for cross-signing.

Welp, time to bring out that xkcd comic out again.
Modern computing systems and devices typically require pieces of crucial open-source software, typically maintained by unpaid or low-paid volunteers. Recently, a report collated a list of critical open-source projects, noting which of them are chronically underfunded and/or understaffed. The information is sobering: 11 out of 23 of the listed projects currently only have one or two maintainers, and funding is generally scarce and sometimes nonexistent.
The Data Drop's report on open-source maintainers identifies that having only one or two sets of eyes on critical pieces of software means that sooner or later something breaks — and it tends to do so in spectacular fashion, given its ubiquity. So, what happens when these projects, which are widely used across software, go underfunded or understaffed?
Lessons from the past
In 2014, the same year as Heartbleed, Shellshock made waves: a vulnerability in the Bash shell that's present in Linux, macOS, and Unix-type systems. articles.title: Las pateras de última generación desbordan a la Guardia Civil en Murcia y Baleares: "No tenemos velocidad para interceptarlas"
articles.summary:
El 2 de septiembre, frente a Cabo Cope (Águilas), una lancha de unos 10 metros y 2 motores ignoró las órdenes de la Guardia Civil. Un agente hizo dos disparos disuasorios. La lancha, en vez de frenar, embistió a la patrullera por un costado y dejó a 3 agentes con heridas leves. Sus ocupantes tiraron garrafas de gasolina al mar y a correr. Llevaban 28.
Detrás de esa escena hay una cifra a destacar: un fueraborda de 350 CV rinde unos 400 Nm, y estas lanchas montan hasta 4. Cruzan de Argelia a Murcia en 3 o 4 horas. Una patera clásica, con 115 o 150 CV, tarda entre 8 y 48. No estás en Motorpasión pero esto te interesa. Al fin y al cabo, todo es física y tecnología.
Persecuciones fracasadas. El secretario de la AUGC en Murcia lo resume en tres palabras: “Nos falta velocidad”. Lo que pide son interceptoras de 55 a 60 nudos, de 102 a 111 km/h. Suena a queja sindical pero es que en el mar es pura aritmética: sin alcance no hay abordaje, ni identificación, ni detenciones, así que se dan a la fuga.
El problema viene de lejos. La barca de madera con un motor que va tosiendo comparte agua con las planeadoras semirrígidas de 10 a 15 metros. Descargan en la playa, giran y vuelven a por el siguiente grupo. El método, según el coronel Pulido, lleva unos 10 años en Murcia. Lo que cambia, dice la AUGC, es la capacidad: hasta 60 o 70 personas por viaje.

OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna and Novo Nordisk.
The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma. In the startup world, there is an ongoing fear that at any moment, the labs will launch new features and become competitors. In this case, Orchestra is getting absorbed, rather than stomped out.

articles.title: Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Agents are breaking AI economics, and the fix starts in the data layer
When companies talk about the cost of artificial intelligence, the conversation almost always starts with models: which one to use, what it costs per million tokens, and whether a smaller model is “good enough.” That made sense when AI meant a chatbot.
It makes much less sense now that agents are doing real work in production. A single agent task can fire off dozens of queries, pull context from several systems, call a model several times and write results back. What a task costs and how fast it runs are increasingly determined by everything that happens around the model.
During a pre-briefing ahead of this week’s expansion of the company’s AI Data Plane, Tim Finley, Couchbase Inc.‘s senior vice president of AI, highlighted a key trend. The company announced native Amazon Bedrock integration with semantic caching, a fully managed Agent Memory and Model Context Protocol server on Amazon Web Services, and vector search in its analytics engine, now called Operational Insights.
The more interesting part is the reasoning behind the release, which points to a problem most information technology leaders haven’t fully accounted for.
Agents are a different kind of user

articles.title: Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
articles.summary:
Assess the entire inference stack — not just open model benchmarks
Impressive benchmark results should make it easy for engineers to select the right open model for the outcome they are tasked with developing. However, that is not the case.
Benchmarks indicate an open model’s optimal performance, but in production, a model must work repeatedly. The challenge is that in production, other factors matter, such as the information provided to the model and its accuracy. So benchmarks can’t tell an engineer whether the AI they are developing will complete the task accurately, or even at all. This is especially important for long-horizon AI tasks.
Ryan Hanrui Wang, SVP of Applied AI at AI cloud provider Nebius, tells The New Stack it is important to measure an open model by the industry benchmarks in conjunction with internal benchmarks and harnesses to ensure you get the inference outcomes the organization requires, something he says the Amsterdam, Netherlands-based company always does in partnership with its clients.
Wang joined Nebius when it acquired Eigen AI, the inference-optimization startup he co-founded and led as CEO, in a roughly $643 million deal announced in May; Nebius sells inference through its Token Factory platform.

articles.title: Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Beyond the KV cache: Training and serving i14’s Laplace 3B linear attention model on AWS Trainium2 with native PyTorch
Most large language models (LLMs) use transformer architectures with softmax attention. During inference, their key-value (KV) cache grows with the conversation or document context. This can reduce concurrency, increase serving cost, and force agentic applications to discard useful history.
i14 designed Laplace 3B as a linear attention alternative. Its recurrent state stays at 29.5 MB per sequence, independent of context length. Working with AWS, i14 used native PyTorch support through TorchNeuron Native to bring this custom architecture to AWS Trainium2. This preserved its Gated Linear Attention (GLA) design and Muon optimizer.
On one trn2.48xlarge instance, Laplace 3B trained at about 120,000 tokens per second. The model served 11,544 output tokens per second across 1,280 concurrent sequences. This post explains the model design, the changes i14 made for Trainium2, and the training and inference results.
About i14
i14 is an AI research and technology company that develops model architectures, components, and runtimes. Its work draws on AI, computational cognitive science, and research into how biological systems learn over time. i14 applies these ideas to models that can retain long-range context without allowing serving state to grow with every token.

articles.title: Chris Lattner: AI Code Generation Doesn't Solve Software Engineering - EE Times
articles.summary:
For AI chip companies, the promise of AI-based coding agents is compelling: generate the low-level kernels needed to get a model running on new hardware, optimize them for performance, and do it without the software engineering resources traditionally required.
But according to Chris Lattner, CEO of AI software startup Modular (recently acquired by Qualcomm, where he now serves as executive VP of software engineering), chip companies should be wary of the limits of AI code generation. Making a kernel run fast is a very different problem from building software infrastructure we can depend on, he told EE Times in an exclusive interview.
“Agents are good, but they’re like anything else; it’s a tool, and you have to use it the right way,” Lattner said. “What I’ve seen with agents is they make tons of throwaway code. So, if you’re building a product, you don’t want to agent-generate everything.”
Agentic code generation makes sense for projects that are well-defined and limited in scope (e.g., “make this kernel go fast”), which can be quantified, measured, and validated, Lattner said, but bigger projects require product design and software engineering and can’t be delegated to agents.
“If you’re a startup and you only care about getting one model working, or getting it to go fast, [then go ahead,] use AI tools to prove it’s possible,” he said. “But that’s not going to be great for when you want to sell your chip to someone else, and they want to run a model you don’t have access to…

Innovasea’s efforts to shrink its embedded system are not simply a packaging exercise. The Canadian company’s devices must be light enough for a fish to carry without materially changing its behavior, yet contain the electronics and battery needed to transmit useful data from underwater. The result is a design problem in which mass, power consumption, and reliability constrain one another.
The Bedford, Nova Scotia-based company develops acoustic telemetry equipment for researchers studying fish movement and behavior. Miniature transmitters travel with the animals; receivers detect their signals.
But that straightforward interaction depends on an engineering effort spanning firmware, acoustic transducers, sensing, and long-duration operation. Jean Quirion, Innovasea’s VP of research and development for fish tracking, describes a business whose products must meet biological requirements as carefully as electrical ones.
“Our customers who are biologists and scientists who are studying these things have rules about the proportion, the weight of the tag, and how that needs to be in proportion to the weight of the fish,” he said in an interview with EE Times. “It’s really not so much about the size; it’s about the actual mass of the tag that needs to be as little as possible.”
That distinction gives miniaturization a specific purpose: allowing researchers to study smaller animals without making the tracking equipment itself an undue influence on what they observe.

articles.title: AI-assisted vibe coding brings Thunderbolt 4 support to Windows 98 SE
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Vibe coding is viewed negatively by many, but when dedicating resources to a specific project isn't feasible, few alternatives exist. Microsoft, for example, doesn't have the time or resources to create modern drivers for operating systems they've long moved on from… but AI has no problem crafting code for legacy versions of Windows.
A developer by the name of Yeo Kheng Meng recently commissioned AI to create a driver that enables generic USB 3.x, USB4, and Thunderbolt 3/4 host controllers to work on ancient operating systems including Window 98 SE, ME, 2000, XP, Vista, and 7.
Dated versions of Windows barely make a blip on the OS market share radar, so why should anyone even care about something like this? Well, despite the low percentage of overall users, there are still lots of retro computing enthusiasts out there actively using older computers running legacy hardware and software. Being able to take advantage of modern connectivity is just icing on the cake for them.
Even if you aren't interested in this particular driver, there's a lot to take away from a story like this. Vibe coding gets trashed in the mainstream as a lazy way to approach a coding problem but as mentioned, not everyone has the time or resources to devote human programmers to every project. Tasks are often tackled based on priority, and making a driver for retro computing fans likely isn't going to rank high on that list.

“We are not forking TypeScript — we are working with the TypeScript team and as a result 7.1 is already ~2.5x faster, too,” Nakazawa writes.

“To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript. We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction.”

International health experts have called the trial “unethical,” but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars.
Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project—an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial. Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy but are currently under investigation by Danish authorities for alleged scientific misconduct.
Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial’s design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Las consultas repetitivas pueden resolverse con rapidez mediante sistemas automatizados; los casos complejos, sensibles o de alto impacto requieren escucha, criterio y capacidad de decisión. El desafío consiste en transferir la conversación a tiempo y sin obligar al cliente a repetir su historia.
Qué consultas conviene automatizar con un bot de IA
Los asistentes de IA resultan útiles para gestiones simples y previsibles: consultar un saldo, verificar el estado de un trámite, actualizar datos, enviar una factura o responder preguntas frecuentes.

articles.title: From backup to energy management: how batteries are changing India's power needs
articles.summary:
From backup to energy management: how batteries are changing India's power needs
As electricity demand rises and renewable energy adoption expands, batteries are evolving from backup devices into critical tools for businesses to manage energy use, improve reliability, and build more resilient power systems.
For years, the conversation around batteries in Indian businesses was fairly straightforward: How much backup do you need?
That question is changing.
In conversations with businesses, channel partners, and people working across the energy ecosystem, I have increasingly noticed that the discussion is moving beyond backup duration. Businesses are asking how they can manage their energy better, protect critical operations, integrate renewable power and reduce their dependence on a single source of electricity.
That shift may appear small, but I believe it signals a much bigger change in the role batteries will play in India's energy system. India's electricity demand is entering a structurally higher-growth phase. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), India's electricity demand is expected to grow at an average annual rate of 6.4% between 2026 and 2030, adding more than 570 TWh to annual consumption over this period. Industry is expected to account for around one-third of this additional demand.

Nvidia wants new AI capacity to show up at the data center fully built. At its GTC Berlin conference on Wednesday, the company introduced DSX POD, a reference design for shipping containers that partners fill with Vera Rubin racks, networking, and liquid cooling before they leave the factory.
Installing and wiring up racks in a conventional data center can take months, Nvidia says. But a DSX POD can be ready to deliver tokens in as few as 14 days, as long as the site already has the necessary power, cooling, and network connections (which are, to be fair, often bottlenecks, too).
The idea here is for data center operators to get to value faster, because, as Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement, “An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete.”
What’s in the box
Each container holds seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, or 504 Rubin GPUs. Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, said in a press briefing ahead of the announcement that a single unit packs about 10 million components and weighs around 28 metric tons.
The containers also come with roughly 20 kilometers of copper cabling and 17 kilometers of scale-out networking preinstalled and tested. Once a container arrives, crews set it in place, connect it to its neighbors, and run the final burn-in tests, Buck said.

articles.title: SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger. The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies.
“Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call.
Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing.
Neither Musk nor his brother Kimbal Musk is independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance.
SpaceX lists six independent directors, including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent director…

articles.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
articles.summary:
Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell
“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”
The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running:
- WordPress 7.1.3
- MediaWiki 1.46.2
- phpBB 3.3.17
- Magento 2.4.9
- Joomla 6.2.0
- Laravel 13.36.0
- Laravel 8.83.29
- Symphony 8.1.9
- Drupal 11.4.10
- WHMCS 9.0.9
All of the above use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.
Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

Braze enables companies to create personalized marketing campaigns for every customer segment. A set of built-in artificial intelligence features, BrazeAI, automatically creates campaign materials such as promotional emails. articles.title: Xbox ya despidió a 1.868 empleados y prepara tres rondas más de recortes hasta enero de 2027
articles.summary:
Xbox despedirá a más empleados este mes, en noviembre próximo y en enero de 2027, según confirmó su CEO, Asha Sharma, en una entrevista con la revista Fortune. La división de Microsoft ya recortó 1.868 puestos de los 3.200 que planea eliminar en un año.
Sharma asumió el cargo en febrero pasado, designada por el CEO de Microsoft, Satya Nadella, para revertir el declive de la marca de videojuegos tras la salida del histórico ejecutivo, Phil Spencer. Desde entonces lidera lo que varios empleados describen como la reestructuración más profunda en la historia de Xbox.
Los próximos recortes se suman a los que ya comenzaron cinco meses después de la llegada de la nueva CEO, cuando la compañía anunció el plan de eliminar el 20% de su plantilla. Entre los despedidos hay empleados que trabajaban en Xbox desde hace décadas, lo que implica, según fuentes citadas por Fortune, la pérdida de conocimiento acumulado dentro de la empresa.
La forma en que se ejecutaron los recortes, repartidos en varias tandas a lo largo de un año, generó además desgaste interno: parte del personal se siente bajo una amenaza constante sobre si su puesto será el próximo en desaparecer.
“No estamos aquí para hacer lo mínimo necesario y tener solo un buen negocio”, dijo Sharma a Fortune. “Estamos acá para ser la empresa de entretenimiento número uno.”

Une première : coincé 491 jours au milieu des mines, ce soldat ukrainien a été sauvé par un drone géant
Les jambes déchiquetées, terré seul au milieu des mines pendant 491 jours, Kostiantyn Vlasenko semblait condamné. Ni fantassins ni robots terrestres ne pouvaient l'atteindre. Pour l'arracher à ce piège, l'armée ukrainienne a tenté un pari qu'elle présente comme une première mondiale : le suspendre sous un hexacoptère lourd et le faire voler au-dessus des lignes russes.
Le 19 octobre, la 92e brigade d'assaut ukrainienne a publié sur Telegram des images saisissantes : un fantassin amputé, harnaché sous un drone à six rotors, survole le front de Koupiansk, dans la région de Kharkiv.
Menée le 4 octobre avec la 30e brigade mécanisée et le fabricant Gurzuf Defence, l'opération a permis de rapatrier Kostiantyn "Magura" Vlasenko, originaire de Kryvyï Rih. Ce soldat tenait la rive gauche de l'Oskil depuis juin 2025. Le 14 février 2026, une munition larguée par un drone russe lui a broyé les deux jambes, au point qu'il a dû s'amputer lui-même. Ravitaillé par les airs tous les quatre ou cinq jours, il a tenu jusqu'au bout.

articles.title: Samsung y SK hynix tienen un problema en China: necesitan modernizar sus fábricas chinas para frenar a YMTC
articles.summary:
YMTC (Yangtze Memory Technologies) está creciendo como la espuma en China. Este fabricante de chips NAND ha alcanzado una cuota de mercado del 38,5% en su país de origen durante el segundo trimestre de 2026, según la consultora Omdia. Durante 2025 su cuota fue aproximadamente del 28%, lo que refleja una tendencia al alza muy marcada. Sin embargo, Samsung y SK hynix, las compañías que lideran el mercado mundial de los semiconductores NAND Flash, se están desangrando en China.
Durante el segundo trimestre de este año Samsung ha retrocedido a una cuota del 33,5% en China. Y SK hynix al 17%. YMTC ya vende más chips NAND Flash en China que Samsung y SK hynix. Y este mercado es demasiado grande y demasiado importante para pasar esta tendencia por alto. De hecho, estas dos compañías surcoreanas están planeando modernizar sus fábricas chinas para competir con YMTC, que ya las ha alcanzado desde un punto de vista estrictamente tecnológico.
Este último fabricante de semiconductores produce sobre todo chips NAND de 160 y 232 capas, pero también fabrica una pequeña cantidad de chips de 294 capas. Y planea superar las 300 capas a medio plazo. Incrementar el número de capas de estos semiconductores es importante porque permite almacenar más información en el mismo espacio, así como reducir el coste por bit. Las plantas que tienen Samsung y SK hynix en China, sin embargo, ya no tienen la capacidad de competir de tú a tú con las de YMTC.

articles.summary:
Connecting the dots: Denuvo has spent the past few weeks trying to uncover Voices38's true identity. The mysterious cracker has been wreaking havoc on the company's notorious DRM and anti-tamper technology, and Denuvo is now turning to lawyers in a bid to unmask the skilled coder.
Denuvo's first attempt to uncover Voices38's real identity was unsuccessful because the company tried to obtain too much data at once. Now, a California federal judge has granted the Irdeto-owned DRM maker's revised subpoena requests. Several internet companies will soon have to respond to Denuvo's lawyers, but Voices38 could still remain a John Doe in the end.
Denuvo's latest legal assault began earlier this month, when the company asked a judge to help identify the unnamed cracker operating under the "Voices38" moniker. The request was part of Denuvo's lawsuit against Voices38, which centers on the cracker's alleged violations of the DMCA's anti-circumvention provisions.
Denuvo initially asked the judge to approve 46 separate subpoena requests targeting Discord, Valve, Reddit, and other internet companies. The subpoenas sought potential names and email addresses, along with additional data related to payments and financial transactions, login logs, comment histories, and more.

articles.title: Building AI in India? Privacy is now a valuation issue: Shivaarti Bajaj
articles.summary:
Building AI in India? Privacy is now a valuation issue: Shivaarti Bajaj
At TechSparks 2026, Shivaarti Bajaj of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm explains why consent, data mapping, and breach readiness under India’s DPDP Act now shape how investors value AI and data-driven startups.
As India’s startups race to build AI-first products, the way they handle personal data could decide what those companies are eventually worth.
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, YourStory’s annual flagship summit, Shivaarti Bajaj, Founding Managing Partner of RSD Bajaj Global Law Firm, argued that privacy can no longer be an afterthought. Founders, she said, are not just shipping products but creating assets: assets that can be valued, bought, sold, devalued, or even taken away if they are not built and complied with correctly.
“When we are creating products, we are creating companies, an asset,” Bajaj said.
Intellectual property remains the first line of defence. Trademarks protect the brands that D2C companies are building, patents matter for deep tech innovation, and copyrights and design protection cover creators, semiconductors, and IoT hardware. But Bajaj noted that IP law in India is well established. The newer and less understood risk lies in the data sets companies collect and create.

articles.title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry.
Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution.
Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes. The catastrophic risk in question must “stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack,” the outlet notes.
The metrics offered here — 50 people and a billion dollars — are similar to those in a piece of California legislation that was recently passed into law, Senate Bill 53, which similarly defined those scenarios as tantamount to “catastrophic risk.”
Anthropic’s bill suggests that analysis of a model’s potential for disaster could be arrived at via the use of “independent evaluators” who would be registered with the U.S. Commerce Department. These evaluators could potentially be paid by the AI labs themselves — so long as the “payment is not contingent on the evaluations’ results,” Politico writes.

articles.title: eMudhra faces scrutiny after weak certificate keys expose flaws in web security
articles.summary:
eMudhra faces scrutiny after weak certificate keys raise web security concerns
Eight weak intermediate certificate keys have prompted browser safeguards and questions over eMudhra’s controls, although the company said customer data and Indian eSign services remain unaffected.
Eight intermediate certificate authority keys linked to eMudhra’s global website-security business were found to be dangerously weak, raising concerns about the systems that browsers use to establish trust online.
The flaw could have enabled attackers to create fraudulent HTTPS certificates and impersonate legitimate websites. The keys were generated on April 30, 2025, but the weakness remained undetected for about 18 months, according to eMudhra’s statement on October 21, 2026.
A certificate authority (CA) verifies identities and issues digital certificates. Intermediate authorities operate under a root certificate trusted by browsers and operating systems.
eMudhra said a key-wrap/unwrap step during its key-generation procedure produced a second, weak set of keys, which were subsequently published to browser root stores. Although the company added its root private key was not compromised, browser operators have withdrawn trust from the associated emSign ECC Root CA - G3 as a precaution.

articles.title: Millions of routers can be hijacked over Wi-Fi thanks to a 16-year-old bug
articles.summary:
Why it matters: Chipmakers ship buggy code all the time, that alone isn't news. What makes WPSplinter stand out is that Broadcom apparently did issue a fix eight years ago, but that fix never reached the routers sitting in people's homes. Furthermore, the lack of a CVE kept the problem invisible to the advisories and patch pipelines that router makers and ISPs rely on.
Security researcher Quentin Kaiser detailed the flaw at the Hexacon conference in Paris on October 16. He calls it WPSplinter, a name he only gave it because Broadcom refused to issue an official identifier.
The bug sits in Broadcom's old code for WPS, the feature that lets you connect a device by pressing a button on the router instead of typing a password. That code mishandles how certain messages are exchanged and with the right sequence of them, it lets an attacker read the router's memory or run external code on the device.
The attacker doesn't need the Wi-Fi password or a completed WPS pairing. Being within radio range is enough. This also isn't the WPS PIN weakness that made headlines in the early 2010s. The problem is Broadcom's code, not WPS itself.
Kaiser's demos make the risk concrete. On an Askey TCG3000 gateway supplied by Orange Belgium, his exploit pulled the Wi-Fi key out of the device's NVRAM, sent it back over the air, and then used it to join the network. On a different device, a Proximus BBOX3V+ made by Sagemcom, he got a remote shell running entirely over Wi-Fi, with no internet connection …

Il était environ 22h40, mardi 20 octobre, quand un Mirage 2000D de l'armée de l'Air et de l'Espace a été accidenté dans le secteur de Rogéville, en Meurthe-et-Moselle. L'appareil de l'escadron de chasse 2/3 « Champagne », basé à Nancy-Ochey, rentrait de mission avec deux aviateurs à son bord. À l’arrière, le navigateur officier systèmes d’armes, ou NOSA, joue le rôle de copilote tactique, en ce qu'il trace la route, surveille les capteurs, comme la nacelle qui pointe un laser sur la cible, et guide les bombes jusqu’à leur objectif. Hier soir, c’est ce tandem qui rentrait de mission.
Selon le ministère, un corps a été retrouvé et attend d’être formellement identifié, tandis que le second membre d’équipage est toujours recherché. Aucune identité n’a été rendue publique.

articles.title: Inception says Mercury 3 beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at up to 8x the speed - SiliconANGLE

Inception says Mercury 3 beats GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at up to 8x the speed
Diffusion language model startup Inception AI Inc. today released Mercury 3, its new flagship model.
In the company’s own benchmarks, Mercury 3 beat OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic PBC’s Claude Haiku 5.5 on eight of 12 tests at four to eight times their speed.
The release takes on the main doubt about Inception’s approach. Co-founder and Chief Executive Stefano Ermon said the question the company has heard most since Mercury 1 “is whether diffusion can scale.” As he sees it, the limits come down to “compute and data, not fundamental algorithmic barriers.”
GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 write their answers the conventional way, one token after another. A Mercury model drafts the whole response up front, then refines every position in parallel over a few passes. Inception clocked Mercury 3 at 1,068 tokens per second on Nvidia Corp. graphics processing units, with Haiku 5.5 reaching about 240 in the same comparison and GPT-6 Luna about 130.
Inception has not disclosed a parameter count for Mercury 3, saying only that it is more than 40 times the size of Mercury 1. The context window grows to 1 million tokens, up from the 260,000 that Mercury 2.5 handled. Ermon said training on Mercury 3’s successor is already under way.

articles.title: Three workers killed, one in intensive care after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident

Three workers killed, one in intensive care after fall at TSMC’s 2nm fab construction site — accident marks at least nine construction deaths since 2024, broken bolt on a steel connection plate suspected as cause behind tragic accident
Four contract workers fell with steel parts during Phase 4 hoisting work, which is now halted.
Three contract workers died, and one more is in intensive care after an accident at the construction site for TSMC’s 2nm Fab 22 in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, reports Taiwan’s Central News Agency. The Southern Taiwan Science Park (STSP) Bureau suspects the cause was a broken bolt on a steel connection plate that sent the workers and steel components tumbling. Steel hoisting on the project has been halted, and the STSP has sent labor inspectors to investigate. The accident is not the first of its kind but rather follows at least a half dozen others since September 2024 at TSMC construction sites in Taiwan, according to local reports. Each of those earlier accidents killed one worker.
Local police said that the men were welding a steel beam on an upper floor and fell with it, while the STSP said the workers were performing steel-structure hoisting and installation when a third-floor connection-plate bolt apparently broke.

Rumor: NVIDIA RTX 6060 May Be Years Away, and Possibly Slower Than the PS6
Anyone holding out for an affordable next-gen NVIDIA card might have a long wait. Hardware leaker Kepler_L2 claims on NeoGAF that the GeForce RTX 6060 will "launch much later," adding that, based on recent trends, he doubts it will even match the PlayStation 6. He was replying to a forum member who argued the PS6 would compete with the RTX 6060, in the same thread where he claimed the console's RAM and storage alone cost over $680. Kepler didn't give an actual date, and the 2029 figure going around seems to be an extrapolation. Both Kepler and kopite7kimi have placed NVIDIA's Rubin-based RTX 60 series in 2028, and the x60 cards usually trail the flagship by a few months. The RTX 5060 arrived under four months after the RTX 5090, while the RTX 4060 took over eight months to follow the RTX 4090. 
With a flagship launch around mid-2028 or later, that could push the RTX 6060 into 2029. That said, the "much later" comment seems to be relative to the PS6, which is reportedly targeting late 2027, so the exact timing is still anyone's guess. Kepler didn't say why, but the ongoing memory shortage looks like the obvious suspect. NVIDIA reportedly postponed its RTX 50 SUPER refresh earlier this year to prioritize AI products that use the same GDDR7 memory, and the company recently admitted that RTX 5090 supply is tight. The update ties into Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, which premiered all ten episodes on Netflix on October 20, and brings new items and features inspired by the anime. So far, CDPR has only teased cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. A first look is coming during a REDstreams broadcast on October 21 at 5 PM CEST, and the official patch notes will go live the same day.
This one is quite a surprise, since Cyberpunk 2077 hasn't received an update in over a year. Update 2.3 arrived in July 2025 with FSR 4, XeSS frame generation, and VRR for consoles, and it looked like the game's final major update at the time. A smaller 2.31 patch followed in September 2025, and the studio has since put most of its focus on The Witcher 4, which has a 2028 release window. Interestingly, 2.31 launched on Switch 2 alongside the other platforms, so the staggered release this time is a bit unusual. CDPR hasn't said anything about PC-specific changes like new upscalers or ray tracing tweaks, so it's reasonable to wait for the patch notes on October 21 before expecting anything on that front.

articles.title: Atlanta doesn't want a real-life RoboCop: City council unanimously backs ban on weaponized robots
articles.summary:
Through the looking glass: We're moving ever closer to a future in which law enforcement controls robots that can kill. But Atlanta has just recommended a new act that ensures this dystopian vision doesn't come to pass: the HALT (Human Authority over Lethal Technology) Act.
Introduced by Council member Liliana Bakhtiari, the act prohibits city employees and contractors, including police, from buying or otherwise acquiring weaponized autonomous systems, drones and remotely operated machines.
In addition to drones, these autonomous killing machines include robot dogs and military-like robots armed with weapons. The act specifically exempts machines used strictly for neutralizing explosives.
"This is about making sure that we are investing in technology with our officers, not replacing them, quite frankly, with 'RoboCop,'" Bakhtiari said.
While we're still not in the era of ED-209 asking people to put down their weapons (then killing them even if they do), Bakhtiari believes the act is a pre-emptive step to ensure this doesn't happen.
The act is also there to stop AI-powered machines from replacing the decision-making of trained Atlanta Police officers. Letting AI make potentially lethal decisions in war is something that militaries have spent years saying would never happen, but that scenario seems closer than ever.
"This is about responsible government, responsible stewardship. It's keeping community at the core of public safety," Bakhtiari told The Atlanta Journal-Constitutio…

Eka offers an artificial intelligence model for robotic manipulation that works from force data as well as camera images. The company calls it a vision-force-action model. Force sensors in a custom gripper tell the model how firmly the hand is holding an object, which lets a robot change its grip partway through a task if something begins to slip. Eka’s announcement cites jobs as varied as packing strawberries and assembling server racks for graphics processing units.
Wired reported in April on a demo of an earlier version of the system at Eka’s office in Cambridge, Mass., where its grippers screwed in light bulbs and packed chicken nuggets onto a moving conveyor. The current robots pick objects that fall outside their training data at about 1,500 operations per hour, according to the company. The human baseline Eka uses for comparison is about 600.
Eka told TechCrunch that its robots handle objects weighing up to 1 kilogram and succeed on more than 95% of picks, and that pilots with industrial customers it has not named are underway on pick-and-place and wire-handling work. The gripper costs less than $1,000 and is rated for 5 million duty cycles for now. Eka wants to reach the 20 million that standard industrial arms are built for.

Members of the operation then used the cards to buy electronics and other merchandise, much of which was shipped to China.

articles.title: Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
articles.summary:
Why you don't need an audiophile headset for gaming — comfort, convenience, and a good mic win over pure audio fidelity
Audiophile headsets are all about audio fidelity — but that's not really what most gamers are looking for.
"Best gaming headset for audiophiles" is one of the categories on our list of best gaming headsets, and it's easy to look at that and wonder if you shouldn't be looking at just audiophile headsets to begin with. Headsets are mainly about audio, after all, and it does seem to logically follow that audiophile headsets would have the best audio (I mean, it's in the name).
Well, not so fast.
Headsets are mainly about audio, but that doesn't mean that the "objectively" best-sounding headset by audiophile standards translates to the best-sounding headset by gaming standards. Nor does it mean that you should choose your gaming headset based on audio quality at the expense of everything else.
Audiophile headsets, including headphones, are primarily designed around one thing: audio fidelity. In other words, they're designed and tuned to reproduce audio exactly as it was recorded, which is exactly as the artist heard it when they were recording it, and is therefore exactly as the artist intended for it to be heard. This doesn't necessarily mean it's going to sound amazing to everyone. In fact, to many people it will probably sound somewhat underwhelming, but it's really the only objective way we have of measuring what makes audio "good," since how something sound…

Safari bloque les cookies intersites depuis six ans, et la publicité en ligne a trouvé un autre moyen de reconnaître les internautes. Apple coupe maintenant l'accès à l'infrastructure qui rend ce suivi possible.
Quand l'adresse email remplace le cookie : ce que Safari bloque
Comme toutes les technique de pistage publicitaire, le mécanisme est particulièrement surnois. Lorsqu'un internaute saisit son adresse mail pour se connecter à un site ou s'abonner à une newsletter, un tiers invisible la récupère et l'envoie à ses serveurs. Ceux-ci l'associent à un identifiant opaque, un code sans lien visible avec vous, et le renvoient au site, qui le stocke. Cet identifiant sert ensuite à vous reconnaître, comme le ferait un cookie, et à vous suivre d'un site à l'autre. Se déconnecter ou se désabonner n'y change rien, puisque l'adresse et l'identifiant restent chez le tiers. Au fil des connexions et des formulaires remplis, celui-ci complète votre profil, ce que le secteur appelle un "identity graph".

Mozilla y Google bloquearon ocho certificados digitales de la empresa india eMudhra después de que un investigador anónimo, identificado solo como Wayne, demostró que podía falsificar la identidad de cualquier sitio de internet.
Los certificados digitales son las credenciales que permiten a un navegador confirmar que una página es quien dice ser y cifrar el tráfico mediante el protocolo HTTPS. Quien controla la clave privada de uno de esos certificados puede hacerse pasar por cualquier sitio web.
Seis de los ocho certificados comprometidos se usan para asegurar conexiones web y los otros dos para firmar programas de software. Todos están respaldados por los programas de confianza de Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple y Google, de los que dependen la mayoría de los navegadores y sistemas operativos del mundo.
El problema no estuvo en el cifrado sino en cómo eMudhra generó las claves. Una clave de ese tipo debería tener alrededor de 384 bits de aleatoriedad, miles de billones de combinaciones posibles. Las ocho claves filtradas tenían apenas entre tres y ocho bits, lo que las hacía recuperables en segundos.
Un ingeniero de Mozilla recuperó las ocho claves por su cuenta en menos de dos horas, sin conocer el método del primer reportante, y confirmó así que la falla era real. Otros investigadores le pidieron a asistentes de inteligencia artificial que resolvieran el problema como si fuera un desafío de seguridad informática, y lo lograron en el primer intento.

La empresa, especializada en ciberseguridad, llegó a esas conversaciones mediante una búsqueda de DNS pasivo, una técnica que registra los nombres de dominio que ya circularon en internet. Abrió solo algunos cientos de los enlaces hallados y dejó el resto sin revisar.
El problema nace del propio diseño de Muse. Cuando un usuario pide compartir una charla con el asistente, Meta genera una página pública y arma la dirección web con el título que el usuario le puso a esa conversación. Ese nombre queda registrado en los servidores de DNS, visibles para cualquiera que sepa buscarlos.
Eso significa que no hace falta recibir el enlace para entrar a la página: alcanza con rastrear los nombres de dominio del servicio, algo que Claroc hizo con una sola consulta a una base de datos comercial. El sitio urlscan.io, que cualquiera puede usar, ya guardaba más de 75 capturas de esas páginas.

El proyecto, desarrollado por Greenhill Forge, logró enfriar una sección del dispositivo hasta los 5 °C (41 °F) mientras la temperatura ambiente rondaba los 16 °C (61 °F), un resultado que el propio canal documentó en video.
La propuesta retoma un principio de ingeniería centenario con una aplicación actual: la posibilidad de generar frío en lugares donde la electricidad es escasa o poco confiable.
El principio detrás del sistema: absorción refrigerante
El dispositivo se basa en la refrigeración por absorción, una técnica que existe desde hace más de un siglo y que prescinde del compresor eléctrico para hacer circular el refrigerante. En su lugar, utiliza calor para impulsar una reacción química que produce el efecto de enfriamiento.
El diseño de Greenhill Forge se compone de dos secciones principales: un generador y un absorbedor. El generador contiene una solución de cloruro de calcio y agua destilada. Cuando el fuego calienta esa mezcla, el vapor de agua se separa de la solución y viaja a través de una tubería hasta un condensador, donde se enfría y vuelve a su estado líquido.
Después, el agua líquida pasa por una pequeña válvula ajustable hacia un evaporador que opera bajo un vacío intenso, de alrededor de seis milibares. A esa presión tan baja, el agua puede evaporarse a tempera…

AMD and Intel will work together to create a single PyTorch code path for AI inference on CPUs — x86 rivals fold AMD ZenDNN library into Intel oneDNN to make CPU AI simpler
AMD has also joined the UXL Foundation as a steering member.
Intel and AMD are integrating their CPU optimizations for PyTorch into a unified library, offering tuning for both AMD and Intel chips through the oneDNN library. AMD has maintained a downstream version of oneDNN called ZenDNN, which is now moving into the open-source oneDNN, published by the UXL Foundation and driven by Intel. AMD also announced it's joining the UXL Foundation as a "steering member," which "influences the future of the UXL Foundation" in exchange for a contribution of $20,000 per year.
AMD says the move to unify these efforts under oneDNN was recommended by the x86 Ecosystem Advisory Group (EAG), which is a joint initiative that primarily exists between Intel and AMD and was established in 2024. The two companies have collaborated through the EAG previously, such as with the ACE extensions for x86 that we learned about earlier this year.
The oneDNN backend is used for CPU inference, and it's built to accelerate that workload for the latest Intel (and now AMD) chips in frameworks like PyTorch. When oneDNN was added to PyTorch as a backend in late 2023, it showed a 1.24x improvement with the Float32 data type, and 2.21x for the BFloat16 data type.

An attacker used a contributor's GitHub account to replace the download archives on five existing releases of OVHcloud's command-line tool on Monday, October 19. The account had been hijacked, and the new files were a build designed to steal secrets stored on the disk of any machine that runs it, the cloud provider says.
They were live on GitHub for up to 94 minutes, from 12:47 to 14:21 UTC, and reached only people who installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI during that window, via a path that checks for no hash, on macOS, Linux x86_64 or arm64, or Windows x86_64.
OVHcloud deleted the swapped archives and published a clean v0.16.0 that evening as an immutable release, whose files GitHub will not let anyone change. The source code, the release tag, and the company's build pipeline were not touched: the bad build was a plain go build of a later commit, uploaded straight onto releases published between April and September.
Who Was Exposed
On v0.15.0, the attacker replaced six files: the macOS x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Linux x86_64 and arm64 archives, the Windows x86_64 archive, and the checksums.txt file, so the published hashes matched the new binaries. The same six files are now gone from v0.11.0 to v0.14.0 as well. The Linux i386, Windows i386, Windows arm64, and WebAssembly builds were left alone on every release.

C'est sur ce raisonnement que repose l'astuce, largement relayée. Sauf qu'aucune preuve technique ne la soutient, et les spécialistes des télécoms sont unanimes pour la réfuter. articles.title: Go Issues Emergency Update Blocking Eight CA Keys Over Undisclosed Security Concerns
articles.summary:
Go 1.27.3 and Go 1.26.10, released on October 20, make Go's certificate verifier reject any certificate chain that passes through one of eight intermediate certificate authority keys.
Programs built on the new release will refuse connections to sites and services whose certificates were issued under those keys. The Go team says the keys belong to one certificate authority it has not named, and that it is blocking them because of "specific security concerns around their operation."
It handled the fix on its URGENT track, the one reserved for its most serious issues, and recommends upgrading immediately.
Two days earlier, on October 17, Mozilla added six intermediate certificates issued by eMudhra's emSign Root TLS CA - G3 to OneCRL, the list Firefox uses to block certificates. The Mozilla bug behind those entries is closed to the public, and neither Mozilla nor Go has said what prompted its action. Whether Chrome, Apple, or Microsoft have taken similar action is not established.
Go's change lists only the SHA-256 hashes of the eight keys. A commenter on the Go issue matched all eight to eMudhra intermediates by looking the hashes up in certificate records.

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.summary:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.

articles.summary:

PlayStation Physical Game Share Still As High As 32%
Since Sony announced that it would be ending physical media production for the PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro, there has been much discussion about the value of physical games media in the modern gaming landscape. Some argue that physical media is invaluable for game preservation and access to content in some remote parts of the world, while others argue that its value is limited, because the physical media market share is small for most games, and it has limited preservation value, thanks to day-one patches. Alinea Analytics recently posted some data about physical media sales on PlayStation, putting more numbers to the impact of physical games media on PlayStation.

articles.title: Eight eMudhra CA Keys Compromised, Triggering Emergency Fixes Across Browsers and Software
articles.summary:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates are compromised, Mozilla and Google's Chrome Root Program confirms on October 20.
An intermediate CA signs the certificates that websites present, so anyone holding one of these keys could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept.
A researcher reported the compromise to the root programs on the evening of October 17, and Chrome and Firefox blocked the eight certificates within hours, after Chrome verified the findings.
No TLS certificate chaining to the six intermediates used for websites had been logged to Certificate Transparency (CT) before Chrome's block, so none could have been trusted by default in Chrome or any other browser that requires CT logging, the Chrome Root Program said.
The keys did not have to be stolen. They were generated with too little randomness, so anyone can compute them from the public certificates, Google's security teams said on October 20. eMudhra said on October 21 that a flaw in the April 2025 ceremony that created the certificates produced a second, weak set of keys alongside the intended ones, and that the weak set is what was published to the browser root stores.
Mozilla recovered the keys on its own within two hours of receiving the report, and researchers have since published them. Whether anyone exploited the flaw since the certificates were created is not known.

Choose agentic AI use cases by measurable business value
Psychologist Abraham Maslow once warned: “It is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.” Agentic AI is becoming the enterprise version of that hammer.

VP of AI transformation at Atos.

Account numbers, balances, passwords, one-time passcodes, card details and government identity numbers such as PAN or Aadhaar are not among the categories the filing lists. Dell CEO Says the Memory Shortage Will Get Worse in 2027
Michael Dell doesn't think the memory shortage is anywhere near over. Speaking with The Wall Street Journal, Dell's chairman and CEO said things will get worse next year, as the AI data center buildout keeps soaking up DRAM and HBM supply. According to him, the bottleneck for Dell isn't demand, since the company is sitting on roughly $95 billion worth of AI server orders it hasn't delivered yet, the largest backlog in its history. Memory is what's holding those shipments back, as AI accelerators need plenty of HBM, while the servers around them still rely on conventional DRAM.
Relief also looks quite far away. New memory fabs take around four years to build, so Dell apparently doesn't expect meaningful new supply until 2029 or 2030. That aligns with Micron's CEO, who recently said supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it is this year. Interestingly, SK hynix's CEO said something similar, expecting the memory shortage to last through 2030. articles.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
articles.summary:
Attackers took control of more than 300 Tor exit relays in early October and used them to redirect SSH connections to servers that stole login passwords, a researcher found.
Exit relays are the last hop in a Tor circuit, where traffic leaves the network for its destination. Only a password login to an SSH server made through Tor between October 1 and 5, after accepting the interception server's host key, could have been captured.
The Tor Project began flagging relays on October 4, and by October 5, none remained in the consensus, the list of relays that Tor clients use. At the peak on October 4, the relays carrying the attacker's exit policy made up 7.46% of Tor's exit capacity, measured by consensus weight, according to an analysis of public Tor directory data posted to the tor-relays mailing list.
The researcher, who publishes as kaba, scanned all of Tor's roughly 3,000 exits on October 2 and found 333 redirecting SSH to the same 12 interception servers. The directory-data analysis counts 377 relays run by 59 operators that switched to the attacker's exit policy between October 1 and 4, which it calls "a policy match, not proof of compromise."
How the Hijacked Exits Intercepted SSH
An exit relay only carries traffic to the ports its exit policy allows. The attackers rewrote that policy in the relays' torrc configuration files to allow port 22 (the SSH port), enabling SSH on 342 relays that had blocked it. Another 24 relays that had not been exits at all became exits.

articles.title: The Harness Is the Hard Part of Agentic Pentesting
articles.summary:
An AppSec team can point an AI agent running on a general-purpose model at its own web apps with little setup. Sure, the model writes the attacks. But everything that makes those attacks safe to run against production and worth acting on afterward lives in the harness around the model. The harness is where the engineering in AI pentesting sits. The Hugging Face intrusion OpenAI disclosed in July showed what happens when that harness gives way, even inside an OpenAI evaluation built to contain the agents.
Why Each Control Takes Rigorous Engineering
Let’s take a closer look at the attack different stages and the role AI agents can take there
Scope
A pentesting agent makes thousands of decisions about where to send its next request, and the model judges each one against a rule written in plain language. A web app’s real boundary often extends past one domain through redirects and calls to outside services. Enforcing scope means code that inspects every request before it leaves, and OWASP’s 2026 guidance routes privileged actions through a deterministic policy engine that checks them at execution time, outside the model.
Credentials
Finding exposed credentials is part of what a pentest does, so the agent regularly comes across working keys outside its assignment. Which of those it may use, for what, and when a person gets involved are policy decisions that the code around the model applies on every attempt.

articles.title: Generative AI Is Erasing Behavioral Tells, Weakening Behavior-Only Detection, Proofpoint Reports
articles.summary:
Generative AI has changed what a malicious email looks like. Messages that once gave themselves away through clumsy wording, generic pretexts, and reused templates now arrive fluent, personalized, and unique to each recipient, and the behavioral signals email filters have relied on for years are fading as a result.
Proofpoint shared several examples of the shift at its Protect 2026 conference. In one, a single threat actor contacted more than 30 real estate agents at the same company, each from a different account, about a different property, and in different words, before closing every thread with the same request: join a video meeting.
Federal data points the same way. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center counted more than 22,000 complaints involving AI in 2025, with nearly $900 million in associated losses, and logged 24,768 business email compromise (BEC) complaints with about $3.05 billion in reported losses, according to its 2025 Internet Crime Report.
What AI Changed
Email filters were built for attackers who had to cut corners. articles.title: Lista de celulares que perderán WhatsApp el 31 de octubre de 2026
articles.summary:
La lista de celulares que perderán WhatsApp el 31 de octubre de 2026 incluye modelos antiguos de Samsung, Motorola, LG y Sony que no alcanzan los requisitos mínimos de la aplicación.
La pérdida de acceso no implica que las cuentas desaparezcan de forma automática. El problema afecta al dispositivo que ya no puede ejecutar una versión compatible del sistema operativo. Quien conserve su número, su copia de seguridad y su cuenta podrá restaurar sus conversaciones en otro teléfono que cumpla las condiciones técnicas exigidas por WhatsApp.
WhatsApp exige Android 6.0 y iOS 15.5 como mínimo
La aplicación de mensajería establece que los equipos con Android deben operar con Android 6.0 o una versión posterior. En los teléfonos de Apple, el requisito señalado es iOS 15.5 o una edición más reciente del sistema. Los móviles que no puedan actualizarse hasta esos niveles perderán la capacidad de instalar nuevas versiones o de mantener el funcionamiento del servicio.
La medida alcanza, sobre todo, a dispositivos lanzados hace más de una década. Muchos ya dejaron de recibir actualizaciones oficiales de sus fabricantes, una situación que limita el acceso a herramientas actuales y reduce las opciones de seguridad. El fin de la compatibilidad responde a la necesidad de que WhatsApp incorpore funciones nuevas sobre sistemas que aún reciben soporte técnico.
No todos los teléfonos antiguos quedarán fuera por la misma razón. Algunos mantienen una versión de Android o iOS cercana al mínimo requerido…

articles.title: "Des scènes qui ne se sont jamais passées" : Emmanuel Macron s’attaque aux images IA du 17 octobre
articles.summary:
En déplacement à Doha, Emmanuel Macron a dénoncé ce mercredi une manipulation étrangère de l’information après les manifestations du 17 octobre. Le président pointe les images générées par intelligence artificielle et s’en prend directement à Donald Trump.
Les images générées par intelligence artificielle qui ont accompagné les manifestations du 17 octobre ont fini par s'inviter au sommet de l'État. Devant la presse ce mercredi 21 octobre à Doha, dernière étape de sa tournée dans le Golfe, Emmanuel Macron a pris soin de séparer ce qui s'est passé dans la rue de ce qui s'est raconté ensuite en ligne, avec notamment la vague d'images IA. Le chef de l’État écarte l’hypothèse d’une ingérence étrangère visible dans les violences elles-mêmes, mais pas dans la manière dont elles ont été racontées en ligne. Il vise au passage plusieurs dirigeants étrangers, Donald Trump en tête.
Depuis Doha, Macron accuse des dirigeants étrangers de relayer des images IA sur la France
Sur les événements récents eux-mêmes, le président Macron dit ne voir « pas d'ingérence étrangère visible ». articles.title: China-Aligned Bronze Sandcastle Abuses Sandboxie DLL Sideloading to Deploy Backdoors
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously undocumented China-aligned threat cluster known as Bronze Sandcastle that has been observed targeting organizations in Asia and Africa since mid-2025.
"The most distinctive technical marker for Bronze Sandcastle is its consistent use of Sandboxie DLL sideloading," Sophos security researcher Gabor Szappanos said in a post published Tuesday.
Between August 2025 and August 2026, attacks mounted by the threat actor have resulted in victims in the Philippines, Taiwan, Afghanistan, Namibia, and likely South Korea. Evidence indicates that Bronze Sandcastle is most active in the UTC+8 time zone.
DLL sideloading is a popular adversarial technique that exploits the way Windows loads DLL files, allowing an attacker to trick a legitimate program into loading a malicious DLL.
When an application is launched, it needs to load various DLLs in order to function correctly. If the application does not provide the full path to a required DLL, the operating system looks for it in a predetermined sequence of directories.
An attacker can take advantage of this behavior by planting a malicious DLL with the same name as a legitimate one in a location that Windows searches before the folder that contains the actual DLL. Thus, when the legitimate application starts, it proceeds to load and run the malicious DLL, giving the attacker a way in to the system.

articles.title: Carros más inteligentes: ahora recordarán correos, mapas y más gracias a la IA de Gemini
articles.summary:
Google comenzó a desplegar una de las actualizaciones más ambiciosas para Gemini dentro de los vehículos: la Inteligencia Personalizada, también llamada Personal Intelligence. La función llega a Android Auto y permite que el asistente consulte correos, fotos, citas y rutas guardadas para responder sin que el conductor dé ningún dato adicional.
Hasta ahora, Gemini respondía en el vehículo de la misma manera para todos los usuarios. Con esta actualización, el asistente accede a la misma información personal que ya usa en el teléfono, lo que multiplica el contexto disponible en cada conversación al volante.
Qué es la Inteligencia Personalizada y cómo conecta los datos con el auto
La Inteligencia Personalizada es la función de Gemini que, con autorización del usuario, conecta de forma segura la información de Gmail, Google Calendario, Google Fotos, Google Maps, YouTube y el historial de búsqueda. Si el conductor tiene una cuenta de Google Workspace, el asistente también puede usar esas herramientas para dar contexto adicional.
El sistema combina dos capacidades: recuperar un dato concreto, como una reserva de hotel guardada en el correo, y razonar sobre varias fuentes a la vez para dar una respuesta completa. Esa combinación es la que permite resolver pedidos complejos sin que el usuario tenga que revisar cada aplicación por separado.
Esta función solo se activa cuando el usuario otorga permiso explícito desde la configuración de Gemini, y puede desactivarse en cualquier momento.…

articles.title: Starfall, la mystérieuse capsule de SpaceX, lancée pour la deuxième fois dans l'espace
articles.summary:
SpaceX vient de lancer Starfall, une capsule qui doit permettre de fabriquer et de tester des produits en orbite avant de les ramener sur Terre. Mais l’entreprise reste encore très discrète sur son vaisseau.
Ce mardi 20 octobre, une fusée Falcon 9 a transporté la charge utile partagée Bandwagon-5 en orbite. À son bord, 32 dispositifs différents, dont une certaine Starfall. Et si SpaceX a expliqué que le déploiement était terminé quelques heures après le décollage, elle n’en a pas dit plus sur son intrigant vaisseau.
Une capsule en forme de disque
Pourtant, Starfall a volé pour la première fois le 23 juin dernier. SpaceX n’avait alors révélé la présence de la capsule que peu avant le décollage, avec pour seul document une image de synthèse. Mais cette fois, elle figurait noir sur blanc sur la page officielle de la mission, aux côtés des clients payants.
Mais à quoi ressemble ce mystérieux vaisseau ? De la forme d’un gros disque, il mesure 3,1 mètres de diamètre pour seulement 0,75 mètre d’épaisseur. Il pèse environ 2 100 kilogrammes et peut ramener jusqu’à une tonne de charge utile sur Terre. Pas de quoi remplacer une capsule habitée, mais assez pour rapatrier des expériences ou des petites productions.

articles.title: Chicago lawsuits claim delivery robots collected personal information without authorization — but the defendants say the allegations are 'frivolous'
articles.summary:
'Sidewalk surveillance': Illinois residents accuse delivery robots of capturing biometric data without permission
Scan and deliver
- Two new Chicago lawsuits claim unauthorized biometric data collections
- In these cases, the biometrics are face and body scans
- Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics have denied the allegations
The backlash to what's perceived as surveillance technology continues, with two Chicago residents taking robot delivery companies to court over the alleged collection of biometric data while dropping off food and groceries.
As the Associated Press reports, the two men bringing the cases claim that robots from Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics turned up — via DoorDash and Uber Eats respectively — even though robot delivery hadn't been requested in the app.
The key allegation is that when these individuals were unlocking the robot cargo bay to get their orders, their hands and faces were scanned via camera and LiDAR technology, without explicit prior permission. If true, that would put Coco and Serve in breach of the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA) of 2008.
Both class-action lawsuits claim that video and sensor data is being retained by these bots in violation of privacy law, and shared with AI companies for training purposes. Statutory damages of $1,000 per negligent violation or $5,000 per intentional or reckless violation are being claimed through the courts.
